jobs.title: Vice President of Technology
jobs.description:
**Summary**

**Vice President, Technology \| Omaha, Nebraska (On\-Site)**


Real Radiology, an established, privately held healthcare services organization, is hiring a Vice President of Technology. The company delivers clinical services to a national client footprint through a distributed provider network. Technology is the operating platform of the business, not a support function, and the company is funding a full modernization of that platform over the next twenty\-four months.


This is a build\-and\-run mandate. You will take ownership of an established technology operation, a funded roadmap, and direct executive sponsorship, and you will be accountable for scaling that into a durable engineering and technology organization.

**What You Will Own**

* Full accountability for technology strategy, delivery, operations, and spend, reporting to the President.
* Replacement and implementation of the core clinical platform, including workflow design, data migration, and cutover.
* The integration layer connecting clinical systems, client systems, and internal applications, including HL7 and modern API\-based interfaces.
* The data platform: warehouse, pipelines, and the analytics and business intelligence layer that leadership and clients depend on.
* Business systems, including CRM, productivity, identity, and document management.
* Information security and compliance operations, including annual certification and remediation against a recognized healthcare security framework.
* Vendor strategy and contract performance across the platform portfolio.
* Applied AI and workflow automation, evaluated on measured operational outcomes rather than pilots.
* Building and leading the internal engineering function, including team structure, hiring, and delivery model.

**The First Twelve Months**

* Take ownership of the core platform decision and drive it to implementation on a committed timeline.
* Establish the engineering function: hiring plan, team structure, and delivery discipline.
* Establish a single operating view of technology cost, risk, and roadmap for the executive team.
* Close outstanding security and compliance remediation items ahead of the next certification cycle.
* Instrument and automate operational workflows to remove manual handling.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Ten or more years in technology, including at least five leading a technology function with full budget and delivery accountability.
* Direct experience in healthcare or another regulated environment where uptime, data integrity, and audit posture are non\-negotiable.
* Demonstrated ownership of a core platform migration from selection through cutover, including the failure modes.
* Track record building or scaling an internal engineering team, including hiring, structure, and delivery cadence.
* Working command of integration and data architecture. You do not need to write production code, but you must be able to evaluate the work.
* Vendor and contract negotiation experience with material commercial exposure.
* Executive presence, direct communication, and a bias toward decisions. Comfort with a short decision path and accountability directly to the executive team.
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with clinical imaging, EHR, or other core clinical workflow systems.
* Experience carrying a security certification through audit and recertification.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
**Role Overview**  

We are seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager to lead a complex mainframe modernization and rewrite initiative through planning, execution, testing, migration, and production go\-live. This individual will be responsible for managing a large, cross\-functional program involving mainframe applications, technology modernization, data migration, integration, testing, business readiness, and cutover. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record leading mainframe rewrite or modernization programs from inception through successful production deployment, with particular strength in managing the final stages of implementation, cutover, and go\-live.  

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the end\-to\-end program delivery for a major mainframe rewrite/modernization initiative, including planning, execution, migration, cutover, and production go\-live.
* Develop and maintain an integrated program plan covering technology, application development, data migration, testing, infrastructure, security, operations, and business readiness.
* Drive the program toward key milestones, ensuring scope, schedule, budget, risks, dependencies, and resources are effectively managed.
* Lead cross\-functional teams consisting of application developers, mainframe engineers, architects, infrastructure teams, QA, data teams, business stakeholders, vendors, and production support.
* Establish and manage the go\-live and cutover strategy, including detailed runbooks, sequencing, dependencies, rollback plans, command\-center procedures, and contingency planning.
* Coordinate multiple testing phases, including system integration testing, regression testing, performance testing, user acceptance testing, and production validation.
* Oversee data conversion and migration activities and ensure reconciliation and validation requirements are met prior to go\-live.
* Manage production readiness assessments and ensure all technical, operational, business, and support requirements are completed before deployment.
* Lead go/no\-go decision meetings and provide executive leadership with clear status, risks, recommendations, and readiness assessments.
* Coordinate the go\-live command center, managing issues, escalations, decision\-making, and communications throughout the deployment.
* Ensure post\-go\-live stabilization, defect resolution, production monitoring, and transition to business\-as\-usual support.
* Proactively identify and manage critical program risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, and interdependencies.
* Manage third\-party vendors and technology partners supporting the modernization effort.
* Prepare executive\-level status reporting, dashboards, steering committee materials, and program communications.
* Drive accountability across workstreams and ensure teams meet committed deliverables and milestones.
* Ensure appropriate governance, change management, documentation, and operational handoff processes are in place.


**Required Qualifications/****Skills*** Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field (Master's degree preferred).
* 10\+ years of experience in program/project management within large\-scale technology environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading mainframe modernization, mainframe rewrite, migration, or transformation programs.
* Proven experience taking a major technology program through testing, cutover, production deployment, and go\-live.
* Strong understanding of mainframe environments and technologies such as COBOL, JCL, DB2, CICS, VSAM, and batch processing.
* Experience coordinating application rewrites, platform migrations, data conversion, and system integrations.
* Strong understanding of SDLC, testing methodologies, release management, and production implementation processes.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing detailed cutover/go\-live plans and production readiness assessments.
* Excellent risk, issue, dependency, and stakeholder management skills.
* Experience working with senior executives and steering committees.
* Strong communication, leadership, organizational, and problem\-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple workstreams and competing priorities within a highly complex environment.


  

**Preferred Qualifications*** Experience with large\-scale financial services, healthcare, insurance, or other highly regulated environments.
* Experience leading programs involving legacy\-to\-modern technology transformations.
* Experience with cloud migration or integration of modern platforms with legacy mainframe environments.
* PMP, PgMP, or similar program/project management certification.
* Experience managing large vendor teams and system integrators.
* Experience leading high\-pressure production cutovers and post\-go\-live stabilization.

 **Locations:** Pittsburgh, PA

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Leadership
jobs.description:
Founded by Dr. Eric Schmidt, the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP) is a 501(c)3 private operating foundation tasked with making recommendations to strengthen America’s long\-term global competitiveness for a future where artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies reshape our global strategic environment. The project is organized into three directorates \- Global Partnerships, Technology Leadership, and AI Adoption. Each directorate will analyze AI and other emerging technologies, address how these technologies will reshape their field and produce detailed recommendations to ensure that America is organized to win the techno\-economic competition.



The Technology Leadership Directorate is seeking a **full\-time Senior Director.** As Senior Director, you will join a team focused on identifying emerging technologies, assessing global competitive landscapes, and developing policy recommendations to strengthen public\-private partnerships. In addition, you will also supervise the implementation of several technology\-focused programs, ranging from private roundtables to public summits and conferences. This role offers exposure to cutting\-edge technologies, national security strategy, and the policy\-making process.



SCSP offers a dynamic work environment, and each employee becomes an integral part of our team. This is an in\-person position at our headquarters in Arlington, VA.



### **Responsibilities**


* Lead a team of Director(s), Associate Director(s), and Research Assistant(s) in Technology Leadership research projects, including providing guidance and tasks focused on technology\-related research projects, including comparative/net assessments, geopolitical analysis, and technological capabilities evaluations.
* Develop and direct the team’s implementation of research plans on strategic technology sectors and methods to gather and analyze relevant industry and government data, government policies , and emerging technology trends, and geopolitical issues.
* Collaborate closely with top experts, high\-level executives, and senior policymakers to evaluate the effectiveness of the American innovation ecosystem and identify gaps relative to U.S. competitors and allies/partners.
* Deliver high\-level briefings, reports, and presentations to communicate research findings and strategic recommendations to senior executives, government officials, and international partners.
* Stay at the forefront of global geopolitical developments, emerging technologies, and other advancements related to the panel’s work, providing timely and insightful analyses to inform strategic decision\-making.
* Foster partnerships with leading research organizations, universities, and industry experts to enhance collaborative research efforts and stay ahead of evolving trends.
### **Minimum Qualifications**


* Master’s or Ph.D. degree in STEM field, international relations, security studies, political science, or a related discipline.
* 10\-20 years of experience in technology and government policy research and analysis, with a proven track record of leading large\-scale research projects and a multidisciplinary team, with a focus on delivering impactful results.
* Deep expertise in technology policy, geopolitical assessments, and strategy development; specific understanding of the techno\-economic competition (e.g., AI, chips, biotech) is essential.
* Demonstrated ability to influence and develop technology policies and strategies, with a deep understanding of international security dynamics and global geopolitical challenges.
* Previous experience in collaborating with government agencies, international organizations, academia, and industry partners is highly desirable.
* Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical skills, and the ability to synthesize complex information into actionable insights for C\-suite leadership and policymakers.
* Outstanding communication skills, including the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and concisely to diverse audiences.
* Excellent leadership and team management capabilities, including mentoring and developing staff members.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey a variety of concepts to diverse audiences.
$160,000 \- $255,500 a year
*This is an exempt position.*

jobs.title: M&A Integration Program Manager
jobs.description:
Join Eaton as an M\&A Integration Program Manager and help drive the successful integration of Boyd Thermal into Eaton. You will translate integration priorities into clear plans, measurable actions, and timely decisions. You will independently manage assigned initiatives while functional workstream leaders remain accountable for their functional deliverables. This position may be performed remotely within the United States, subject to Eaton’s remote\-work requirements. The role requires periodic travel to Eaton and Boyd Thermal locations and regular collaboration across regions and time zones. Candidates must be comfortable travelling up to 25% of the time domestically and internationally.

  

The expected annual salary range for this role is $113000 \- $165000 a year. Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.


**What you’ll do:**
-------------------


You will coordinate cross\-functional plans, milestones, risks, and executive reporting while partnering with leaders across functions and regions. This highly visible role offers broad exposure to post\-merger integration, business transformation, and enterprise program management.
  

  

• Coordinate integrated workplans, milestones, deliverables, and critical\-path activities across assigned functional workstreams.
  

• Independently manage selected integration initiatives from planning through execution, ensuring owners, due dates, dependencies, and expected outcomes are clear.
  

• Maintain accurate program information in Eaton’s designated integration\-management systems, including milestones, actions, risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies.
  

• Identify cross\-functional conflicts, delays, and emerging risks; work with stakeholders on mitigation plans and escalate decisions through the appropriate governance forums.
  

• Prepare concise status reports, dashboards, executive briefings, and presentation materials for Integration Management Office and executive governance reviews.
  

• Facilitate working sessions and governance meetings by developing agendas, documenting decisions, assigning actions, and driving timely follow\-through.
  

• Coordinate the planning and sequencing of Transitional Service Agreement exits, capability stand\-up activities, target operating\-model changes, and other integration priorities.
  

• Partner with functional, communications, and change\-management leaders to support stakeholder engagement, readiness, training, and adoption activities.
  

• Analyze program data and performance indicators to identify trends, improve visibility, and recommend actions.
  

• Capture lessons learned and improve integration tools, templates, processes, and reporting practices for use in future acquisitions.


**What a typical week may include**
-----------------------------------

  

  

• Updating integrated project plans, milestones, and dashboards.
  

• Following up with functional owners on actions and deliverables.
  

• Preparing an executive integration update.
  

• Facilitating a cross\-functional risk or dependency review.
  

• Coordinating TSA\-exit or operating\-model readiness activities.
  

• Analyzing program data and identifying emerging issues.
  

• Partnering with change and communications teams on stakeholder readiness.
  

• Improving an integration template, tracking tool, or governance process.

-------------------

• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
  

• Minimum five years of experience in program or project management, management consulting, business transformation, operational excellence, continuous improvement, or post\-merger integration.
  

• Candidates must be capable of travelling up to 25% of the time domestically and internationally.
  

• Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F\-1 to H\-1B, H\-1B cap registration, O\-1, E\-3, TN status, I\-485 job portability, etc.
  

  

**Preferred qualifications**

• PMP, CAPM, Prosci, or another relevant project or change\-management certification.
  

• Experience developing executive\-level and working\-team communications for different audiences.
  

• Experience with program dashboards, portfolio\-management tools, Power BI, SharePoint, or comparable platforms.
  

• Experience working in a global, matrixed organization.
  

• Experience facilitating cross\-functional meetings and driving actions to closure.

Department Information

Together, we innovate for a stronger Colorado

The work of employees at the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is challenging and diverse because the needs of agencies, customers and Coloradans constantly evolve. But our focus never changes: improve the lives of all Coloradans through innovation and collaboration. We're building one of the nation's leading government IT organizations by reimagining how we support agencies, building first-of-their-kind applications, and creating an inclusive, collaborative culture, together. Join us in the important work of providing equitable access to services.

Watch this video to learn more about how we're Serving People. Serving Colorado.

Description Of Job

IMPORTANT NOTE:

Please review your application to ensure completion. For the most equitable applicant experience, OIT’s hiring team considers only the contents of your application to review your qualifications. Please do not include any attachments (such as resume or cover letter) with your application as these items are not used by OIT’s hiring team.

The Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology is in the middle of a transformation worth joining. We're building cross-functional pod teams that partner directly with agencies to design, deliver, and continuously improve services that work for Coloradans. Good government depends on technology that works. And OIT exists to make that true for every Coloradan. The State of Colorado is seeking a Director, Technology to help build the next generation of public services. We're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers in service of the public.

The Director, Technology is the Leader in OIT’s agency service model. You will determine the appropriate approach in working with OIT and Agency executives in aligning and implementing OIT and agency business needs. This position operates proactively as a strategic partner, embedding in agency planning before problems surface, rather than reactively as a service provider. You will build credibility with agency leadership quickly and maintain it through demonstrated delivery. The role oversees technology used to support all aspects of any supported agency's technology needs and collaborates with agency leadership as a strategic partner to provide in-depth technical expertise in support of business decisions.

What You'll Do...

Communicate and translate between technology initiatives and mission requirements with senior agency stakeholders, including Executive Director, CFO, and program leads.
Facilitate discussions with agency stakeholders and operational staff to identify competing priorities and elicit clear decisions.

Extensive experience with guiding teams that manage projects and programs following Agile Methodologies

Proven ability to influence stakeholders and build consensus, collaborating and communicating effectively across all levels of the organization.

**Exponent** is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.

Reporting to college leadership, the Program Manager serves as the operational anchor and primary administrative leader of the PROSPECT project.

Overview of the Position This full\-time position is in the Clerk’s Office of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court, Northern District of Illinois and reports to the Clerk of Court. The Director of Information Technology is responsible for managing and overseeing automated systems within the court, including the operation, coordination, and integration of all Judiciary and local applications. The incumbent is responsible for managing the Information Technology Department and primarily directs supervisors and oversees the coordination, training and integration of office automation equipment, telecommunications, and courtroom technology. The Director of Information Technology is a forward\-thinker who explores development opportunities regularly to expand and enhance IT staff skill sets, keeping the department on the cutting edge of new and improved technologies. You will shape the technical vision and grow into owning the architecture of a cloud platform built on hundreds of Java microservices that process millions of real\-time transactions every day.  

  

You will join a mature, high\-volume platform that is already running in production. You'll spend your first 90 days learning it deeply, embedded with the teams that built it, and take ownership of its architecture domain by domain: starting with the data and transaction layer, then service architecture and the cloud platform. By the end of your first year, you'll own the platform's architecture end to end and set its direction for the years ahead.

You must be comfortable explaining technology strategy and trade\-offs to executives, business partners, and regulators.

* Expert\-level Java (Java 17\+), with deep knowledge of Spring Boot / Spring Cloud, concurrency, and JVM performance tuning and garbage collection.
* Proven track record designing and operating a microservices estate of 100\+ services in production.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Southern Tier Library System is accepting applications for the position of Director of Information Technology. The library system seeks an energetic candidate with a robust understanding and vision for 21st century technologies in the field of public libraries, and a passion for providing meaningful services to 48\-member libraries within a team\-based, cooperative library system environment.

**GENERAL STATEMENT OF DUTIES** 

This is an administrative, full time, exempt, professional position charged with overall management of the Division of Information Technology. Under the general direction of the Executive Director, the Director of IT oversees successful implementation of all operations within the Division of Information Technology. Additionally, this position provides support to member libraries relative to all aspects and approaches of technology services, requiring a sound technical background including knowledge in computer systems, networking, storage systems, databases, applications, security and protecting sensitive data from external threats.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE POSITION** 

Staff Leadership \& Service Delivery

* Direct and supervise IT department staff, including the PC Deployment Technician, Systems Specialist, and Network Specialist.
* Assign projects, establish priorities, and monitor completion.
* Provide technical guidance and escalation support to staff.
* Coordinate IT services delivered to member libraries.
* Approve timesheets, benefit time, and staff scheduling.
* Identify staff training and professional development needs.
* Develop cross\-training and succession coverage for critical systems.

Technology Planning \& Infrastructure Management

* Establish the organization's technology strategy and infrastructure direction.
* Oversee servers, virtualization, networking, cloud services, storage, backup systems, and data\-center infrastructure.
* Plan infrastructure upgrades and replacement cycles.
* Ensure appropriate system capacity, availability, performance, and reliability.
* Design and maintain disaster\-recovery and business\-continuity capabilities.

* AWS and Heroku

jobs.description:
**SUMMARY**  

Concord Academy, a boarding and day school for grades 9 through 12, is located in historic Concord, Massachusetts, less than 20 miles from Boston. Known for its intellectually curious students, accomplished faculty, and deeply relational approach to education, CA is creating a new director of technology position to provide dedicated internal leadership for a technology program long supported by school employees, department leaders, and external partners. For an accomplished technology leader, this is an opportunity to join a distinctive school at an important moment, build from a dependable foundation, and help to connect different technology initiatives at the school under one roof.  

For more than a decade, two internal technology professionals and a team of professionals from OunceIT, CA’s longtime managed\-service provider, have worked together to maintain daily service, advance infrastructure, guide systems work, and develop substantial institutional knowledge. As departments have adopted specialized platforms, integrations, data flows, and support pathways, technology decisions have become more complex. The transition to Veracross, now underway, has made the need for coordination more visible. CA now needs one internal leader who can take responsibility for the full technology environment, coordinate people and partners, recommend strategic priorities for technology that reflect CA’s institutional goals, and make systems and services easier to navigate for students, faculty, staff, and families.  

Concord Academy seeks a technically grounded, hands\-on leader who can address immediate operational needs while helping the school prepare for the future. The successful candidate will be comfortable guiding complex projects, leading and developing staff, managing vendor relationships, working with academic leaders, and explaining technical matters clearly to the school community. jobs.title: Senior Staff Technical Program Manager, ESS
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Sr. Staff Technical Program Manager, ESS


**Location:** San Francisco Bay area, CA


**Department:** ESS Engineering


**Reports to:** CTO


**Position Type:** Full\-time

  


**About the Company**



Peak Energy is the first American venture to advance globally proven Sodium\-Ion battery systems as the storage standard for the new era of renewable energy on a resilient grid.



Sodium\-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market.



Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt\-level innovation at world\-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, SunPower, Fluence, and Enovix. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures.



We are a team of engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience.

  


**About the Role** **– Sr. Staff Technical Program Manager**



Peak Energy is looking for a Sr. Staff Technical Program Manager to lead the end\-to\-end development and delivery of our sodium\-ion energy storage systems across hardware and software.



Reporting to the CTO, this leader will serve as a key partner to the technical leadership team, helping translate company and product priorities into clear development plans, driving critical technical decisions, and ensuring risks and dependencies are surfaced and resolved early.



You will build and lead a lean team of Technical Program Managers while remaining close to the work. The right candidate will be comfortable operating at multiple levels: shaping the overall product\-development operating model, coaching TPMs, leading critical programs directly, and engaging deeply enough in technical discussions to improve the quality and speed of decision\-making.

  


**What** **You'll** **Do (****Responsibilities****)**


* Own integrated program execution from architecture and requirements through verification, industrialization, and customer delivery.
* Build, lead, and develop Peak's Technical Program Management team.
* Partner with the CTO and engineering leaders to translate product strategy into clear priorities, plans, milestones, and decisions.
* Drive system\-level integration across ESS hardware, cells, software, firmware, manufacturing, supply chain, and field deployment.
* Lead cross\-functional trade\-offs involving performance, safety, reliability, cost, scope, schedule, and manufacturability.
* Establish clear requirements, interfaces, verification plans, release criteria, and program ownership.
* Identify and resolve technical, organizational, and schedule risks before they become critical.
* Provide clear, decision\-oriented communication to executive leadership.
* Build lightweight, scalable program processes that improve execution without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
* Step directly into critical or off\-track programs when hands\-on leadership is needed.


**What You'll Bring (****Qualifications****)**


* Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
* 12\+ years leading complex technical programs or product\-development organizations.
* Experience taking hardware or software\-enabled hardware products from concept through production.
* Experience building and leading teams of Technical Program Managers or equivalent technical leaders.
* Strong technical judgment across system architecture, requirements, integration, verification, and production readiness.
* Demonstrated ability to lead difficult trade\-offs across technical and business constraints.
* Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and drive accountability without direct authority.
* Ability to operate across strategy, organizational leadership, and hands\-on execution in a fast\-paced environment.
* Eligible to work in the United States.


**Preferred Qualifications**


* Experience in battery energy storage, electric vehicles, robotics, aerospace, industrial equipment, or another complex hardware industry.
* Familiarity with battery systems, embedded software, controls, power electronics, energy management systems, or grid integration.
* Experience in safety\-critical, regulated, or reliability\-intensive product development.
* Experience scaling products and organizations from early development through production and commercial deployment.
* Experience partnering closely with a CTO, VP of Engineering, or equivalent technical executive.

  



Peak Energy is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We strongly encourage women, people of color, and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. We value skills, potential, and perspective over specific credentials. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't look perfect on paper, we still want to hear from you.


**Our Core Values**


* **Speed Through Focus** \- Move fast but understand why. Focus on the goal, don't sacrifice quality.
* **Mission Over Self** \- It's about the greater good; confident humility. Take ownership and accountability.
* **Face the Brutal Truth** \- Transparency, honesty, big picture curiosity. Fearless decision making.
* **Be a Good Person** \- Kindness, collaboration and teamwork.

  


**Compensation \& Benefits**



The salary range for this role is $200,000\-$260,000, with actual pay varying based on work location, experience, and skills. Our competitive benefits package includes:


* Flexible time off
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
* Strong 401(k) plan
* Equity opportunities
* Many great work perks


Join us to thrive in a supportive environment while making a meaningful impact in the energy sector!

jobs.title: Director of IT - Restaurant Systems
jobs.description:
We’re not just another chicken joint—we’re one of the fastest\-growing brands in the game, built on hand\-made food and bold ambition. At Slim Chickens, every tenderloin gets the royal treatment: brined, buttermilk\-soaked, hand\-breaded, and cooked fresh to order. That same care and craft goes into how we grow our people.


If you’ve got hustle, heart, and an entrepreneurial spark, this is the place to prove yourself and shape your career. Our team thrives on real connection—working fast, thinking big, and building something that makes an impact every day. Here, you’ll be trusted to make decisions, empowered to own your work, and part of a crew that’s taking this brand to the next level.


Slim Chickens is growing fast. The only question is—are you ready to grow with us?

**PURPOSE OF THE POSITION**


As the Director, IT Restaurant Systems at Slim Chickens, you're responsible for establishing the company's IT strategy and roadmap for restaurant technology, leading and project managing core restaurant technology projects, and overseeing day\-to\-day support, implementation, and management of the company's technology infrastructure at both the restaurant and corporate levels, including but not limited to Point of Sale, Back Office, and related systems.




**ESSENTIAL POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technology/Software Implementation**

* Leads the IT strategy and roadmap for all restaurant technology (POS, BOH, Digital Menu Boards, Mobile App, etc.) to comprehensively plan and lead future technology initiatives and projects that meet company objectives.
* Leads execution and project management of all core IT projects end to end, from initial concept and strategy through development, testing, pilot, deployment, and post\-deployment support, including internal resources, contractors, and vendors.
* Leads the implementation of the company's POS and Back Office technology solutions with minimal disruption to operations.
* Leads and manages an IT Support Analyst team (2 FTEs) overseeing all POS and Back Office database management, including but not limited to menu items (core and LTOs), inventory, and labor management.
* Collaborates with internal teams and franchisees to ensure project goals and timelines are met.
* Oversees the annual PCI compliance review.
* Leads deployment and management of internal IT tools (Monday.com, Claude, etc.).
* Provides training, guidance, and mentorship to employees and direct reports.
* Manages the IT budget.

**Technical Support**

* Provides restaurant and leadership teams with ongoing support of IT platforms.
* Oversees day\-to\-day management of all core IT platforms and restaurant technology vendors.
* Establishes process and structure for IT technical support teams end to end, from troubleshooting issues to reporting metrics and performance.
* Keeps detailed records of issues to help the company identify and address the sources of common problems.
* Provides clear, concise communication and documentation for all teams.
* Ensures IT team members are knowledgeable and fulfilling their responsibilities to end users.

**Growing the Brand**

* Supports all new restaurant openings and remodels related to IT systems, including configuration of new locations in restaurant systems (CrunchTime, Brink).
* Participates in the selection, testing, and implementation of new hardware and software platforms to support continuous improvement in the technology infrastructure for our guests.

**IT Strategy**

* Establishes both short\-term (6–12 month) and long\-term (3–5 year) roadmaps for restaurant technology.
* Manages project timelines and expectations as set forth by leadership.
* Proactively seeks out new technology that can give the company a competitive advantage.
* Effectively evaluates how new technology will complement existing solutions and business practices.

**Project Management**

* Leads key technology projects end to end (concept, sourcing, development, pilot, deployment, and post\-deployment support) to solve business problems, improve guest experience, and improve franchisee profitability.
* Coordinates with department leadership to prioritize and scope solutions that fit company goals, and collaborates cross\-functionally to ensure project success.
* Collaborates with the franchise system to ensure IT strategy and project goals are aligned and met.
	+ Maintains and monitors corporate project management tools (Monday.com), including admin, accessibility, and vendors supplying third\-party project management support.
	+ Maintains and monitors corporate AI licenses, including admin, accessibility, and usage limits.

**IT Budget**

* Assists in managing the IT budget to stay within target.
* Monitors and reports any related issues or concerns.
* Manages IT projects and timelines to ensure budget expectations are met.




**Slim Chickens systems principles and objectives:** Has a thorough understanding of Slim Chickens' established operating systems (e.g., quality, security, office environment, company policies, safety) and recognizes the responsibility to stay updated on these systems and the role this position plays in supporting them.

**Performs other duties as necessary in support of business objectives:** This position description is designed to guide the activities of the Director, IT Restaurant Systems. It is not meant to restrict the individual's creativity or limit their thinking, nor does it encompass all the tasks that may be required in this role.

**Physical Activities:** Primarily performed in an office environment. Involves entering and retrieving information on a computer and visually verifying details, often in small print. May also require presenting information to small or large groups.

**Travel:** Occasionally requires travel to multiple restaurants or work sites, which may include overnight stays.

* Willing to challenge themselves and others and move out of their comfort zone.

-----------------------

**What you'll do...**
---------------------

**Role summary:**
  

At Walmart, we are people\-led and tech\-powered. The MyWalmart platform team owns and delivers the enterprise platform that powers the daily work lives of 1\.6 million store associates nationwide. We build, support, and evolve intuitive tools that simplify store workflows, reduce operational friction, and keep associates connected to what matters most. In close partnership with store operations, product, and engineering teams, the MyWalmart platform team combines strategic program execution, operational discipline, and associate advocacy to deliver reliable technology that makes store work easier and helps our associates better serve our customers.
  

**About the team:**
  

Walmart is people\-led and tech\-powered. As Director, Technology Operations, you will lead the strategy and operational execution for the MyWalmart platform. You will build, mentor, and inspire a high\-performing team of technology operations professionals, fostering a culture of accountability and growth. In this role, you will partner closely with senior business and technology leaders to align strategic roadmaps with frontline store needs. Leading cross\-functional collaboration across product, engineering, and retail operations, you will ensure the delivery of dependable tools that simplify daily routines while maintaining disciplined program execution.
  

**What you'll do:**
  

* Lead operational strategy and program delivery for the MyWalmart platform, aligning technology initiatives with enterprise business priorities.
* Partner with senior business, operations, and technology leaders to shape multi\-year roadmaps and translate strategy into store\-floor results.
* Build, mentor, and inspire a high\-performing operations team centered on accountability, operational excellence, and talent development.
* Collaborate across product, engineering, and store operations to streamline associate workflows, manage performance metrics, and drive data\-backed improvements while mitigating operational risk.


  

**What you'll bring:**
  

* Proven leadership in building, mentoring, and developing high\-performing technology operations and program management teams.
* Track record of partnering with senior business and technology executives to influence strategy and align priorities across matrixed organizations.
* In\-depth experience driving large\-scale technology initiatives and translating complex business goals into clear operational execution plans.
* Demonstrated expertise in establishing performance metrics, leveraging data to drive continuous improvement, and proactively mitigating operational risks.
* Exceptional communication skills with the ability to build consensus, advocate for associate needs, and deliver results at scale.


At Walmart, we offer competitive pay as well as performance\-based bonus awards and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet. Health benefits include medical, vision and dental coverage. Financial benefits include 401(k), stock purchase and company\-paid life insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO (including sick leave), parental leave, family care leave, bereavement, jury duty, and voting. Other benefits include short\-term and long\-term disability, company discounts, Military Leave Pay, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, and more. You will also receive PTO and/or PPTO that can be used for vacation, sick leave, holidays, or other purposes. The amount you receive depends on your job classification and length of employment. It will meet or exceed the requirements of paid sick leave laws, where applicable. For information about PTO, see https://one.walmart.com/notices. Live Better U is a Walmart\-paid education benefit program for full\-time and part\-time associates in Walmart and Sam's Club facilities. Programs range from high school completion to bachelor's degrees, including English Language Learning and short\-form certificates. Tuition, books, and fees are completely paid for by Walmart.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Interim Housing
jobs.description:
**Hope Mission Statement**


The mission of Hope the Mission is to prevent, reduce and eliminate poverty, hunger, and homelessness by offering immediate assistance and long\-term solutions.

**Position Purpose and Summary**


Our interim housing sites are a connection point for participants, staff, community partners; and funders who set expectations for excellence. The Program Manager is responsible for all of it.


Reporting to the Director of Interim Housing or Senior Director of Programs, the Program Manager is the main leader at the site level. They are responsible for day\-to\-day operations, supervising staff, keeping participants safe, and making sure the site meets all contract requirements. This role sets the standard for how services are delivered, how staff show up, and how the site runs — not just during regular hours, but across every shift, in every interaction, and under the close watch of every funder. When something goes wrong, the Program Manager responds. When paperwork falls short, the Program Manager fixes it. When a participant's path to permanent housing slows down, the Program Manager makes sure the team has what it needs to move things forward.


This role covers a lot of ground. It includes managing people, monitoring compliance, responding to incidents, coordinating across departments, representing the organization in the community, and overseeing services that keep participants at the center. All of this happens in programs that run around the clock and serve people dealing with serious instability. That is not by accident. Interim housing is complex, and the Program Manager is the person Hope the Mission trusts to lead it well. The quality of leadership at this level determines whether HTM's sites are places where people feel safe, supported, and moving toward something better — or just places where people stay.

*Participant Services and Outcomes** Oversees participant\-centered service delivery grounded in Housing First, Harm Reduction, and Trauma\-Informed Care principles
* Coordinates with internal departments, community partners, Coordinated Entry System (CES) stakeholders, and public agencies to support participant outcomes and system alignment

*Cross\-Departmental Coordination** Collaborates with Finance, Facilities, HR, IT, Development, and Compliance teams to ensure timely reporting, budget tracking, procurement, facility readiness, and administrative requirements are met
* Serves as a key point of contact for high\-level communications to volunteers, leadership, and other stakeholders
* Facilitates special events with interdepartmental coordination and volunteer engagement

Company Description

Deen Capital is a quantitative investment manager specializing in U.S. public equities, combining data-driven research with an ethics lens informed by Islamic investing principles. The firm uses systematic, rules-based multi-factor models—such as quality, value, momentum, and profitability—to guide stock selection and risk management. Deen Capital applies Islamic-principled screens to avoid businesses that conflict with Islamic ethics and to limit exposure to excessive leverage and interest-centric activities. Its investment process emphasizes risk-aware portfolio construction, diversification, liquidity considerations, and disciplined drawdown management, supported by transparent and continuously tested research. Deen Capital serves investors and advisors seeking U.S. equity exposure managed with quantitative rigor and faith-aligned values.

jobs.description:
The Superconducting Technology Architect is a Director-level technical leadership role within the GF Labs Technology Architecture organization. This role defines and advances foundry platforms for superconducting qubits, Josephson-junction digital logic, cryogenic control and readout, and related integration. The position requires deep technical expertise, platform leadership, and the ability to translate emerging system requirements into scalable, manufacturable technologies.

Job Summary

The Superconducting Technology Architect leads the definition, development, and delivery of superconducting quantum and digital technologies and associated customer programs. The position integrates device, process, design, test, packaging, foundry operations, and program execution; guides internal and external R&D; and serves as a senior technical and customer-facing authority for GF leadership and partners.

Essential Responsibilities

Develop and influence long-term roadmaps for superconducting qubits, SFQ-family digital logic, cryogenic control and readout, parametric amplifiers, interconnect, and packaging.
Translate customer and system requirements into materials, process flows, device structures, design rules, PDK content, test vehicles, and acceptance criteria.
Shape manufacturable qubit technologies spanning Josephson junctions, resonators, couplers, readout, low-loss materials and interfaces, coherence, fidelity, variability, and yield.
Define scalable digital platforms, including RSFQ, ERSFQ/eSFQ, RQL, and AQFP, addressing junction uniformity, timing, wiring, inductance, power, memory, thermal budgets, and cryogenic I/O.
Lead process integration, experiments, simulations, tape-outs, cryogenic characterization, technology transfer, qualification, and new-product introduction across superconducting logic, qubits, cryo-CMOS, multi-chip modules, TSVs, flip-chip, and heterogeneous integration.
Build and govern internal and external development programs with customers, universities, research organizations, government laboratories, suppliers, and startups, including technical scope, proposals and estimates, milestones, schedules, budgets, IP, and transition plans.
Lead multidisciplinary engineering and program teams; recruit and mentor talent; drive quality, schedule, budget, and customer commitments; and communicate architecture choices, execution status, risks, and investment priorities to customers and GF executives.
Drive foundry operational improvement through cycle-time reduction, SPC and control-plan maturity, manufacturing systems, process quality, program reviews, and schedule-risk reduction.
Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.

Required Qualifications

Education: MS or PhD in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Materials Science, or a related discipline.
Years of Experience: 15+ years in semiconductor technology, superconducting electronics, quantum hardware, or advanced process integration, including leadership of complex technology programs.
Deep expertise in Josephson-junction devices, superconducting qubits and/or digital logic, cryogenic operation, RF/microwave circuits, materials and interface loss, and device-to-system tradeoffs.
Demonstrated success translating architectures into foundry processes and transferring technologies from research into fabrication, qualification, or manufacturing, with ownership of quality, schedule, budget, and customer deliverables.
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary engineering and program organizations and strategic collaborations across customers, research organizations, suppliers, startups, and matrixed internal functions.
Percentage of travel: 20%.

Preferred Qualifications

PhD with industrial experience in superconducting qubits, superconducting digital electronics, Josephson-junction fabrication, or cryogenic system integration.
Experience with transmon-class qubits, microwave resonators, control/readout, parametric amplifiers, decoherence mechanisms, and cryogenic measurement.
Experience with SFQ-family circuit design, simulation, layout, timing, and 3D electromagnetic modeling; familiarity with RQL is beneficial.
Knowledge of superconducting materials and junction processes, multi-chip modules, thermal or superconducting TSVs, flip-chip interconnect, heterogeneous integration, cryo-CMOS, cryocoolers, wafer-scale integration, and cryogenic packaging.
Experience with proposal development, technical basis-of-estimate, integrated schedules, Agile execution, manufacturing systems, SPC, control plans, and customer or executive program reviews.

jobs.description:
The Senior Manager, IGA is a senior technical and client-facing leadership role focused on driving Identity Governance and Administration engagements from strategy through execution, with SailPoint and Saviynt as core platforms of expertise. This role requires the ability to lead technical architecture design sessions directly with clients – translating complex governance, compliance, and identity lifecycle requirements into scalable IGA target-state architectures. While IGA is the primary focus, the ideal candidate also brings working knowledge of adjacent IAM domains, including Privileged Access Management (PAM) and Access Management (SSO/MFA), to design cohesive, end-to-end identity solutions. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to client stakeholders, architect enterprise-grade IGA solutions, and lead cross-functional delivery teams, while also contributing to business development, proposal development, and practice growth.

Key Responsibilities

Lead technical architecture design sessions directly with clients, translating business, security, and compliance requirements into scalable IGA target-state architectures.
Architect and oversee end-to-end implementation of Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) solutions using SailPoint and Saviynt as primary platforms.
Design and lead delivery of core IGA capabilities, including identity lifecycle management (Joiner/Mover/Leaver), access certification/attestation campaigns, role-based access control (RBAC) and role mining, Segregation of Duties (SoD) policy design, entitlement management, and access request/approval workflows.
Lead application onboarding strategy for IGA platforms, including source/target connector design, birthright and non-birthright provisioning, and integration with authoritative HR sources
Define and implement IGA governance frameworks, including policy design, audit and compliance reporting, and global configuration/data segmentation best practices.
Working knowledge of adjacent IAM domains – Privileged Access Management (PAM, e.g., CyberArk, Delinea) and Access Management (SSO/MFA via Entra ID, Okta, Ping) – to ensure IGA architectures integrate cleanly across the broader identity ecosystem.
Own end-to-end delivery for engagements, managing scope, timelines, technical quality, and client satisfaction.
Serve as the primary technical point of contact for clients, running architecture workshops, discovery sessions, and executive-level readouts.
Develop maturity assessments, governance roadmaps, and target operating models tailored to client environments and industry (e.g., healthcare, higher education, financial services).
Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and career development to IAM engineers, architects, and consultants on the delivery team.
Partner with sales and account teams on business development activities, including solution scoping, proposal/SOW development, and technical presentations for prospective clients.
Advise clients on regulatory and compliance considerations (e.g., SOX, HIPAA, GDPR) as they relate to identity governance controls, certifications, and audits.
Monitor emerging IGA trends and best practices (including AI-driven governance) and champion their adoption across client engagements.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field.
10+ years of hands-on IAM experience with a strong concentration in Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), including consulting or client-facing delivery, and at least 3-5 years in a technical leadership or architecture role.
Deep, hands-on expertise architecting and implementing SailPoint and Saviynt, including certification campaigns, RBAC/SoD design, connector configuration, and workflow customization.
Strong understanding of identity lifecycle management, entitlement governance, access certification processes, and provisioning/de-provisioning across enterprise applications.
Working knowledge of PAM concepts and platforms (e.g., CyberArk, Delinea, BeyondTrust) and Access Management/SSO technologies (e.g., Entra ID, Okta, Ping) sufficient to architect integrated IAM solutions.
Proven ability to lead technical architecture discussions and design sessions directly with client stakeholders, including CISOs and IT leadership.
Solid understanding of identity protocols and standards, including SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SCIM, and LDAP.
Experience managing project resources, timelines, and deliverables across multiple concurrent engagements.
Demonstrated experience mentoring and developing technical teams, with strong people leadership skills.
Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and executive audiences.
Relevant certifications strongly preferred (e.g., CISSP, CISM, SailPoint Certified, Saviynt Certified Professional).

jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

In the digital economy, it takes more than good ideas and strong leadership to thrive. Upgrading outdated processes, systems and information is vital – but can be a risky investment in such a rapidly changing environment. That's why some of the most prestigious businesses worldwide look to us for authoritative, agile, and efficient solutions for business decision-making. As a ServiceNow Consulting Senior Manager you will play a leading role in that mission, providing the competitive edge our clients need to overcome some of the biggest creative and technical challenges around.

The opportunity

You will lead ServiceNow Transformation teams in a rapidly growing area of the business. It is a client facing role, in which you will have opportunities to showcase your ability to not only motivate and develop teams but also establish and maintain client relationships. You will have an opportunity to grow your consulting, technical and team leadership skills, as well as build relationships and obtain experiences that will define your career.

In this role, you will build and manage the delivery of technology transformation projects and programs that align with our organizational strategy. You will provide assurance to leadership by managing timelines, costs, and quality, while leading both technical and non-technical project teams in the development and implementation of technology solutions and infrastructure.

Your Key Responsibilities

As a Senior Manager, you will play a pivotal role in the effective management and delivery of complex processes, solutions, and projects. You will navigate operational and organizational dynamics while maintaining a strong focus on quality and risk management. This position offers a unique opportunity to develop your leadership skills and expand your professional network. Key responsibilities include:

Leading engagement delivery and managing client relationships on a daily basis.
Accountable for program/project management, ensuring that all objectives are met.
Developing resource plans and budgets for engagements, managing engagement economics effectively.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Here, you’ll serve a wide portfolio of clients - each with their own backgrounds, strengths, and ambitions, so no two days will be the same. That could mean working to improve our customers’ IT/OM Asset Management process or evaluating how AI can streamline delivery. Wherever you find yourself, you’ll be making a visible impact on projects that cross borders and challenge conventional wisdom to encourage transformation. To thrive in this role, you will need a blend of technical expertise and strong interpersonal skills. The following attributes will make a significant impact:

Ability to drive and support sales activities along-side EY pursuit teams demonstrating how EY's services can solve a clients business challenges – this can include but not limited to developing proposals, engagement estimates, and participating in sales presentations
Lead and develop strategies for ServiceNow enabled transformations, working with senior client executives on developing a business case, transformation roadmap, detailed plans and solution architectures
Act as an engagement manager across all aspects of a ServiceNow IT/OM Asset Management project and solution delivery including but not limited to design, configuration/development, testing and deployment phases
Ability to manage 2-3 engagements and mentor multi-disciplinary teams of 10+ resources including offshore resources (e.g., consultants, developers, and testers)
Ability to build and foster client relationships and demonstrate the value of EY services
Excellent business acumen with the ability to make fact-based decisions and resolve conflicts
Provide guidance and industry leading practice expertise for ServiceNow IT/OM Asset Management process implementations, including how specific business objectives can be met through process and technology transformation
Ability to analyze a company’s IT/OM Asset Management people, process, and technology capabilities, provide leading practice recommendations and contribute insights to strategic roadmaps
Ability to advise on the connectivity of the CMDB and IT Operations Management (ITOM) to ITSM processes
Experience with ServiceNow AI capabilities, including Now Assist, AI Agents, and AI Control Tower, and their application across ITAM, HAM, SAM, OT asset management, and CMDB-driven workflows
Familiarity with Armis or similar OT/IoT asset intelligence platforms to support asset discovery, risk context, vulnerability prioritization, and ServiceNow workflow integration
Ability to shape AI-enabled asset management roadmaps that improve asset visibility, compliance, lifecycle risk management, operational resiliency, and business value
Ability to lead client process design sessions and facilitate requirements workshops with functional and/or business process area subject matter resources
Experience in waterfall and agile delivery models – including supporting management activities such as planning, status reporting, budgets and risk and issue logs
Ability to create high-quality deliverables and project artifacts

To qualify for the role you must have

Bachelor’s degree required (4-year degree); Master’s degree preferred
Typically, no less than 5 - 7 years relevant experience in ServiceNow implementation experience
5 – 7 years of Big 4 or equivalent consulting experience preferably at the Senior Manager or Director level
ServiceNow Certified Systems Administrator (CSA) or Certified Application Developer (CAD)
Minimum of 2 of the following ServiceNow certifications:
ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Hardware Asset Management
ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Software Asset Management
ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Data Foundations

Excellent consulting and interpersonal skills – executive communication (written/verbal), adaptability, problem solving, teamwork, relationship building, dependability, and organization
Ability to effectively develop presentations, functional and technical roadmaps as well as present ideas and proposals to all levels of management and technical expertise
Experience with defining contextual, conceptual, and logical models that align both business and technical capabilities to explain the architecture
Experience leading teams and supervising others
A driver's license valid in the U.S (United States).
Ability to travel to meet client needs (up to 60%)

Ideally, you will also have

ServiceNow Certified Master Architect (CMA) or Certified Technical Architect (CTA)
ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Discovery
ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Vulnerability Response
Performance analytics and reporting experience – certifications are a plus
Experience in ServiceNow’s AI solutions (Now Assist, Agentic, AI Control Tower)
Experience with Armis and other OT asset tracking platforms (e.g., Nozomi)

What We Look For

We are interested in intellectually curious people, with a genuine passion for finding and implementing innovative ways to nurture growth. You will also need excellent communication and negotiation skills, as well as the ability to express big ideas to senior leaders, often without technical backgrounds. If you are ready to take ownership of a team that is poised to take the industry by storm, this role is for you.

What We Offer You

At EY, we’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences. We’ll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. Learn more.

We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. The base salary range for this job in all geographic locations in the US is $171,600 to $392,100. The base salary range for New York City Metro Area, Washington State and California (excluding Sacramento) is $205,900 to $445,700. Individual salaries within those ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. In addition, our Total Rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.
Join us in our team-led and leader-enabled hybrid model. Our expectation is for most people in external, client serving roles to work together in person 40-60% of the time over the course of an engagement, project or year.

jobs.description:
We strongly encourage people of color, transgender and non-binary people to apply. HRC is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes everyone, including non-LGBTQ+ people, to join our team. Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that people from marginalized communities are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At HRC, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Position Summary

The Human Rights Campaign is a large, national nonprofit civil rights and advocacy organization working to advance equality for LGBTQ+ people. Technology is essential to that work. It enables our staff to organize, advocate, collaborate, and work effectively with partners, volunteers, and communities nationwide.

As Director, IT Operations, you will lead the technology environment that makes that work possible: secure, reliable, well-managed, and easy to use. Reporting to the VP of IT & Data Analytics, who leads enterprise technology strategy and digital transformation, you will serve as HRC’s technical and IT operations leader. You will translate strategy into a practical technology roadmap and lead IT operations, service delivery, enterprise systems, workplace and event technology, operational security, the internal IT team, and our managed service and technology partners.

This is a broad, hands-on operational leadership role in a lean nonprofit setting, not an infrastructure specialty. Success in this role requires balancing strategy, service delivery, vendor management, operational leadership, and technical decision-making. While technical credibility is important, the role is not intended to personally perform all engineering, administration, or support work. Instead, the Director is responsible for ensuring successful outcomes through a combination of internal staff, managed service partners, and other technology vendors.

We are looking for a leader who combines technical credibility with strong people leadership, clear communication, sound judgment, and a commitment to excellent service.

You will build trusted relationships with business owners and internal stakeholders, help teams navigate technology and process changes, simplify and modernize our technology environment, strengthen the IT team and its operating practices, and ensure technology effectively supports HRC’s mission.

Position Responsibilities:

IT Leadership & Modernization
Develop and execute an IT operations and modernization roadmap aligned with organizational priorities, informed by strong partnerships with program owners and internal stakeholders.
Serve as the senior technical advisor for IT operations, evaluating technical options, dependencies, risks, and vendor recommendations.
Lead efforts to simplify legacy and overlapping technologies and advance a secure, cloud-first operating environment.

IT Operations & Service Delivery
Lead day-to-day IT operations across identity and access, endpoints, cloud and infrastructure, productivity and collaboration platforms, and IT-managed enterprise applications.
Ensure effective delivery of technology services through a combination of internal staff, managed service providers, security partners, and technology vendors, establishing clear ownership, accountability, and service expectations.
Establish and mature IT service management practices, including incident, problem, change, knowledge, and asset management, with clear service standards, accountability, and governance. Ensure technology changes are communicated, documented, and managed to reduce operational risk and improve coordination across internal teams and technology partners.
Drive root-cause analysis and durable resolution of recurring technical and service issues.
Lead technical planning and execution for migrations, integrations, upgrades, consolidation, and retirement of legacy technologies.
Ensure technology services are secure, reliable, and operationally ready, including appropriate lifecycle management, patching, backup, and disaster recovery.
Ensure reliable technology and AV support for hybrid meetings, Board meetings, and major organizational events through appropriate planning, resourcing, thorough testing, and coordination of internal and external support resources, providing hands-on support when necessary.

Vendor Management & Cybersecurity
Serve as the primary owner of managed service and key technology partner relationships, establishing clear service expectations, governance processes, reporting, escalation paths, and accountability for outcomes.
Evaluate vendor performance, service quality, and value realization, making recommendations regarding service improvements, scope changes, or provider transitions when appropriate.
Manage IT contracts, licensing, renewals, and technology operating expenditures within approved budgets.
Partner with fractional CISO and cybersecurity service providers to operationalize security controls, incident response, vulnerability remediation, data protection, and risk-reduction priorities.

People Leadership & Communication
Lead, coach, and develop the internal IT team, setting clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, communication, customer service, and follow-through.
Assess team capabilities and recommend appropriate staffing, role design, training, and use of external expertise.
Communicate technical issues, risks, options, and changes clearly to staff, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders to reduce change management challenges

Perform other related duties as required to support organizational operations, major initiatives, and events.

Position Qualifications:

At least 10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years managing IT operations, service delivery, or comparable enterprise technology functions.
Demonstrated leadership experience managing across multiple IT domains, including identity and access, endpoint management, cloud/infrastructure, enterprise applications, and end-user technology services.
Strong working knowledge of modern identity and endpoint management, including experience supporting both Windows and macOS environments.
Experience managing cloud-based productivity, collaboration, and SaaS environments, including Microsoft 365 and/or Google Workspace.
Strong IT service management experience, particularly incident, problem, change, knowledge, and asset management, with demonstrated success improving service quality and resolving recurring issues.
Proven experience managing MSPs and technology vendors, including service levels, escalations, root-cause analysis, remediation, contracts, and performance accountability.
Experience working with cybersecurity teams or providers to implement security requirements and address operational risks, including identity and endpoint security, vulnerability remediation, incident response, and data protection.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing IT staff, setting clear expectations, building accountability, and improving team performance.
Experience implementing technology roadmaps and managing complex migrations, modernization efforts, or other significant technology initiatives, including stakeholder engagement, communication, and organizational adoption.
Strong technical judgment and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to assess cross-platform issues, identify root causes, evaluate technical recommendations and tradeoffs, and make sound technical decisions.
Ability to build trusted relationships with senior management on technical options, risks, dependencies, and operational implications to inform technology planning, prioritization, and investment decisions.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues, risks, decisions, and expectations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to balance hands-on technical involvement with staff management, delegation, vendor oversight, operational priorities, and longer-term initiatives in a lean IT organization.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience modernizing complex or hybrid environments toward simplified, cloud-based services.
Familiarity with Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Azure, AWS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or comparable technologies.
Familiarity with recognized cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST CSF or CIS Controls.
Experience supporting distributed workforces and external stakeholders such as contractors, volunteers, or partners.
Experience in nonprofit, advocacy, or other mission-driven organizations.
Knowledge of or interest in LGBTQ+ issues, and a demonstrated commitment to a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace.

Work Environment & Availability

This position is located at HRC Headquarters in Washington, DC, and requires regular on-site presence of at least four days per week. The role is generally performed during standard business hours but requires flexibility to support organizational events, critical system needs, and operational priorities that may occur in the evenings, on weekends, or on holidays. While the Director is expected to be available for significant incidents and major organizational events, day-to-day operational coverage is shared across internal staff, managed service providers, and established support processes.

All positions at the Human Rights Campaign and/or the Human Rights Campaign Foundation may require regular or periodic travel. Where business travel is required, appropriate compensation as outlined by the Fair Labor Standards Act will apply.

For more information, please visit our website at www.biocryst.com or follow us   on LinkedIn and Instagram .

Job Summary

BioCryst is a fast-growing pharmaceutical company seeking an experienced Associate Director, IT Business - Partner Pharmaceutical Development to build and mature strategic partnerships across Development. The role supports Program & Portfolio Management, Clinical Development / Operations, Biometrics, Pharmacology / Non-Clinical, Regulatory, Safety, and Medical Affairs. The IT Business Partner will understand functional strategies and operating needs, translate them into technology roadmaps and prioritized initiatives, and enable compliant, scalable process and system improvements across the development lifecycle. This role serves as a strategic technology advisor and delivery leader, with responsibility for business analysis, program and project leadership, solution design, data and integration strategy, vendor management, adoption, and ongoing application support. The role requires working knowledge of key Development platforms and capabilities, including Veeva RIM, Veeva CTMS, ReadCube, clinical data visualization and analytics solutions, and the Oracle Argus safety system. Please note: this role can be remote working east coast with a strong preference for the Boston, MA area.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Serve as the primary IT Business Partner and trusted technology advisor for Program & Portfolio Management, Clinical Development / Operations, Biometrics, Pharmacology / Non-Clinical, Regulatory, Safety, and Medical Affairs.
Build strong partnerships with functional leaders and subject matter experts to understand strategies, business capabilities, pain points, risks, and priorities.
Translate business priorities into multi-year technology roadmaps, business cases, demand plans, and sequenced delivery portfolios.
Lead demand intake, discovery, requirements definition, solution evaluation, prioritization, implementation, adoption, and value realization for Development technology initiatives.
Provide subject matter expertise for the selection, implementation, enhancement, integration, and support of Development applications and data capabilities.
Partner with business and IT stakeholders to optimize platforms including Veeva RIM, Veeva CTMS, ReadCube, clinical data visualization and analytics solutions, Oracle Argus, and related Development systems.
Develop a working understanding of Development processes and data flows, including clinical study operations, regulatory information and submissions, safety and pharmacovigilance, biometrics, non-clinical activities, processes, and medical information or evidence-generation needs.

Ensure GxP and other regulated applications are implemented and maintained in accordance with applicable validation, data integrity, privacy, security, change control, and records-management requirements.
Oversee system lifecycle activities, including application ownership, release management, vendor upgrades, incident and problem management, access governance, business continuity, disaster recovery, and application retirement.

Partner with Clinical, Biometrics, and Data and Analytics teams to improve access to trusted study information and strengthen clinical data visualization, reporting, and decision support.
Lead cross-functional programs and projects, managing scope, schedule, budget, resources, risks, dependencies, decisions, communications, and executive-level status reporting.
Manage strategic technology vendors and managed service providers, including performance, service levels, delivery quality, contracts, and issue escalation.
Drive user adoption through stakeholder engagement, communications, training, process documentation, and change-management activities.
Monitor emerging technologies, including automation, analytics, and responsible AI, and recommend practical opportunities that support Development priorities and compliance expectations.
This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. The role leads and manages MSPs, contractors, vendors, and consultants, as needed, for project implementation, project delivery, and ongoing system support.

Demonstrated experience as an IT Business Partner, product owner, application leader, program manager, or similar role supporting Development or R&D business functions.

Experience with regulated GxP computerized systems, including validation, data integrity, audit trails, electronic records and signatures, security, change control, and inspection readiness.

Experience with system integrations, data flows, vendor-hosted platforms, and external partners such as CROs and managed service providers.

Experience leading contractors, and external partners in a matrixed and cross-functional environment.

Ability to manage multiple priorities, navigate ambiguity, influence without direct authority, and work effectively both as a leader and as a contributing team member.
