You’ll provide second\-line oversight of complaint processes without taking ownership of routine complaint handling.
You’ll maintain the enterprise Fair Lending and UDAAP risk\-assessment and monitoring framework, analyze outcomes and exceptions, document issues, and provide objective challenge where potential discrimination or consumer harm may exist. You’ll also provide second\-line review and escalation for marketing, advertising, disclosures, campaigns, and Member communications, working within clear boundaries so content owners retain responsibility for accuracy, approvals, and implementation.
Another important part of the role is helping the organization manage compliance risk as things change. Before new or modified products, services, systems, channels, vendors, disclosures, or Member journeys are implemented, you’ll perform second\-line compliance risk assessments, document conditions, challenge unresolved risks, and escalate material concerns through established governance.**Giving Leadership a Clear View of Compliance Risk**
-----------------------------------------------------


Strong compliance programs depend on information leaders can understand and act on. You’ll maintain the enterprise compliance issue inventory, assign risk ratings and escalation thresholds, monitor corrective\-action commitments, and prepare concise reporting for management committees, Senior Leadership, and the Board or an appropriate Board committee.
You’ll also facilitate the collection of compliance materials for regulatory examinations and compliance audits, coordinating request logistics, evidence control, and finding tracking with Audit and Controls or other designated partners.
Throughout the work, you’ll maintain clear boundaries between the second line and other functions. You’ll collaborate with BSA/AML/OFAC, Fraud Risk, Operational Risk, Legal, Information Security, and Internal Audit while maintaining the independence required of a second\-line risk function.
When significant or unresolved compliance exposure arises, you’ll use independent judgment, provide documented challenge, and escalate appropriately to the VP, Enterprise Risk Management and established governance committees.

--------------------------

### **Experience**

* Demonstrated experience leading or materially supporting an enterprise\-wide Compliance Management System or second\-line compliance program within a regulated financial institution.
* Experience challenging and advising senior business owners across lending, deposits, payments, marketing, digital, operations, and Member\-facing channels while maintaining constructive relationships with Legal, other risk functions, and Internal Audit.

**Position Summary**


Credence has an upcoming need for a Senior Program Manager who will be primarily responsible for supporting the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center WAM (AFLCMC/WAM) directorate, F\-16 division at WPAFB, OH.


F\-16 “Viper” AFLCMC/WAM is headquartered at Hill Air Force Base with units located at Wright\-Patterson Air Force Base, Tyndall Air Force Base, Eglin Air Force Base, and Davis\-Monthan Air Force Base. The F\-16 “Viper” is a multi\-role fighter jet delivering air\-to\-air, air\-to\-ground, and surveillance capabilities for the United States Air Force (USAF) and Coalition Partners.


The F\-16 program has the largest Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program in U.S. history producing over 4,500 jets for 24 countries. Each F\-16 FMS case is uniquely tailored to country requirements / development / funding. Presently, FMS production orders exist through 2030\. Additionally, the F\-16 program includes the Multi\-National Fighter Program (MNFP). MNFP is not a typical FMS program, but a unique, cooperative USAF and development program implemented through the FMS process under the framework of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Tech Integration, Global Energy Sustainability & Automation (GESA)
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------


The Technical Program Manager (TPM), Technology Integration \& Support is responsible for the end\-to\-end onboarding, integration, and deployment of automation vendor technologies (AGVs, AMRs, autonomous floor care, etc.) across Amazon's fulfillment and sortation network. This role serves as the primary technical liaison between external vendors and internal Amazon stakeholders — ensuring that all vendor technologies meet Amazon's network, security, and compliance standards before deployment.  

  

Key job responsibilities  

Vendor Technology Onboarding (40%)  

* Own the full lifecycle of vendor IT onboarding for AGV/AMR and automation technologies — from initial kick\-off through production deployment
* Conduct technical kick\-off meetings with vendor engineering teams to review Amazon IT requirements (network architecture, security, IoT device standards)
* Guide vendors through Amazon's onboarding documentation process: network diagrams, IT overview questionnaires, data element inventories, and wireless device assessment forms
* Manage 4–5 concurrent vendor onboarding projects at steady state; scale to 10\+ during peak periods
* Track onboarding status across all active vendors using Asana and/or SmartSheet dashboards


Network Architecture \& Configuration (20%)  

* Review and approve vendor network diagrams for compliance with Amazon network standards
* Configure VLANs, assign static IPs, generate PPSKs (pre\-shared keys) for WiFi 802\.11ax connectivity
* Coordinate ACL port configurations and firewall rule deployments with local IT and network engineering teams
* Validate that vendor IoT devices operate within approved frequency bands, protocols, and power levels


Security \& Compliance (15%)  

* Manage Third\-Party Security (TPS) assessments with Amazon InfoSec — submit tickets, gather vendor responses, track remediation
* Author and submit ANOW (Access Network Operations Workflow) requests for vendor network access
* Coordinate IoT device certification through Amazon's hardware qualification pipeline
* Ensure vendor technologies meet mTLS, SSO, and SiteConnect/VPN requirements before go\-live


Technical Assessments \& Documentation (10%)  

* Author formal Vendor Technical Assessment reports evaluating integration risk, network impact, and deployment readiness
* Document conditional approvals, pilot constraints, and scaling requirements for each technology
* Maintain a centralized knowledge base of approved devices, network configurations, and onboarding playbooks


Infrastructure Deployment Coordination (10%)  

* Coordinate physical infrastructure work with general contractors (GCs) — network rack installation, LVC/power cabling, IPC housing, fire alarm panel integration
* Develop and distribute BOMs (Bills of Materials) for site\-level technology deployments
* Establish and run weekly coordination meetings for multi\-site rollouts


Cross\-Functional Stakeholder Management (5%)  

* Serve as the single\-threaded owner for vendor IT integration across legal, category management, IT security, safety, demand intake, and local IT teams
* Manage escalations from site teams, EU/international stakeholders, and Amazon leadership
* Provide regular status updates to program leadership on vendor onboarding pipeline health

  

A day in the life  

A Day in the Life  

Every day as a Technical Program Manager on the Technology Integration \& Support team brings a dynamic mix of technical problem\-solving, vendor collaboration, and cross\-functional coordination. Here’s what a typical day looks like:  

You start your morning by reviewing your Asana and Taskei dashboards to check the status of 4–5 active vendor onboarding projects. You flag any blockers — maybe a vendor’s network diagram needs revisions before it can be approved, or a Third\-Party Security (TPS) assessment is awaiting InfoSec feedback. You prioritize your day around what will keep these projects moving forward.  

By mid\-morning, you’re leading a technical kick\-off call with a new AGV vendor’s engineering team. You walk them through Amazon’s IT requirements — network standards, security protocols, IoT device certification — and outline the onboarding documentation they’ll need to complete. You answer their questions about VLAN configurations, WiFi 802\.11ax connectivity, and mTLS requirements, translating Amazon’s standards into actionable steps for the vendor.  

After lunch, you shift into hands\-on technical work. You review a vendor’s submitted network diagram for compliance, configure VLAN assignments and static IPs for an upcoming pilot site, and generate PPSKs for wireless device connectivity. You coordinate with the local IT team on ACL port configurations and firewall rules that need to be deployed before the vendor’s equipment arrives on\-site.  

In the afternoon, you join a weekly coordination meeting for a multi\-site robotics rollout. You provide updates on the technology integration workstream, review the Bill of Materials for the next site, and align with general contractors on network rack installation timelines. After the meeting, you draft a Vendor Technical Assessment report evaluating a new automation technology’s integration risk, network impact, and deployment readiness.  

Throughout the day, you’re the single\-threaded owner connecting the dots between vendors, site teams, IT security, legal, and program leadership. You might field an escalation from a European site team about a connectivity issue, submit an ANOW request for vendor network access, or update leadership on the health of your vendor onboarding pipeline. No two days are exactly the same, but every day centers on making sure the right technology gets integrated safely, securely, and on schedule.  

  

About the team

jobs.description:
Job Description

As a global technology leader, Honeywell Process Technology (PT) enables the energy evolution, provides solutions that reduce emissions, and delivers innovative sustainable materials to our customers across industries. We are committed to driving sustainable practices and enhancing energy efficiency through cutting-edge technology and innovative solutions. Our team is dedicated to creating a sustainable future by empowering industries to transition toward cleaner energy sources and reduce their carbon footprint. Join us in our mission to make the world a more sustainable place while delivering exceptional value to our customers.

As Director of IT for OT, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering technology capabilities that enable resilient, efficient, and scalable supply chain and plant operations across PT. Leadership & Financial Management

Lead and develop a high‑performing, multi‑disciplinary global team across OT, setting clear expectations and driving accountability for results.
Lead the M&A Infrastructure, Operations and Security Team
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement, enabling teams to deliver results in a fast‑paced, matrixed environment.
Own and manage OT technology budgets, ensuring investments are aligned with PT business priorities and deliver measurable value and return on investment.
Establish and monitor KPIs and value realization metrics, making data‑driven course corrections to ensure operational, financial, and strategic objectives are met or exceeded.

Qualifications

Must Haves

A minimum of 8 years of experience in IT infrastructure management and/or ISC platforms.
Proven experience managing OT initiatives.

WE VALUE 

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Master's degree in IT or related field
Leadership experience in two or more Information Technology, Engineering or Strategy functional areas 
Proven experience leading ERP transformations
Strong understanding of network architecture and security principles.
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Proven ability to drive strategic initiatives and foster collaboration across cross-functional teams.
Familiarity with compliance standards and regulations related to IT infrastructure.
Strong technical, quantitative, and analytical skills 
Experience in the manufacturing or chemical industry
Knowledge of cybersecurity and data privacy best practices Project management certification (e.g., PMP)
Understanding of key information technology solutions and practices 
Strong business/financial acumen and ability to translate new technology into business value 

The annual base salary range for this position in Illinois is $177,000 - $221,000. This position is incentive plan eligible. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Technology Risk Management (Cyber Threat & Insider Risk)
jobs.description:
Your opportunity

At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together. We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

As Schwab continues to expand its technology footprint across cloud, artificial intelligence, digital platforms, applications & APIs, and infrastructure services, the Technology Risk Management (TRM) team plays a critical role in helping ensure the company maintains a strong risk posture through independent oversight and risk-informed assurance activities.

TRM has an opening in the Cyber Threat & Insider Risk discipline for an individual contributor to serve as the primary subject matter expert for second line oversight, effective challenge, and risk reporting of Security Operations, Digital Forensics, and Incident Response capabilities, processes, and controls. More specifically, this role reviews risks and control activities over cyber detection, monitoring, investigation, containment, and response. You will assess control effectiveness, identify systemic weaknesses, and ensure alignment with enterprise policies and standards, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices. You will review and challenge issue identification, closure, risk acceptances related to risks in your domain. You will maintain visibility into the firm's emerging threats and implementation of AI technologies and influence the implementation of expected monitoring, investigation, and response control activities. Success requires a self-starter attitude, strong desire to learn, building collaborative relationships with business partners, and the ability to assess and communicate technical risk clearly to executive, committee, regulatory, and technical audiences.

Please note: This position is Monday through Friday during standard business hours and follows a hybrid work model with four days in the office and one day working from home. The role is available only in Indianapolis, IN; Omaha, NE; Austin, TX and Southlake, TX (DFW). Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate at their own expense to one of the listed locations.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

What you have

To ensure that we have fulfilled our promise of "challenging the status quo," this role has specific qualifications that successful candidates should have.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in Risk Management, Cybersecurity, or Internal Audit
Demonstrated Risk Assessment, Risk Identification, and Risk Prioritization experience
Ability to apply Analytical Thinking and Problem Solving to complex technology risk information
Strong Communication skills with the ability to present clear conclusions to technical and executive audiences
Demonstrated Collaboration and Stakeholder Management Influence skills across multiple functions and organizational levels

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or an equivalent technology risk, cybersecurity, audit certification
Experience identifying and assessing risks associated with security operations, digital forensics, and/or cybersecurity incident response
Financial services industry experience
Demonstrated Self-Starter, Influencing Others, and Building Collaborative Relationship competencies in an evolving environment

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time**Description**
---------------


At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history \- from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.  

At the heart of Defining Possible is our commitment to missions. In rapidly changing global security environments, Northrop Grumman brings informed insights and secure technological solutions to enable strategic objectives. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi\-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. By joining in our shared mission, we will support yours by expanding your personal network and developing skills, whether you are new to the field or an industry thought leader. At Northrop Grumman, you will have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career.

  

Northrop Grumman's CIDO Project Management Office (PMO) and the Multi\-Domain Operations Division, Missile Defense Integration Business Unit, is seeking a **Sr Principal Chief Information and Digital Office (CIDO) Program Manager**. This position may be located in Colorado Springs, CO or Boulder, CO. Travel between sites is expected.  

  

  



The Chief Information and Digital Office (CIDO) Project Management Office for Space Sector plays a critical role in delivering technology and digital solutions across the business. To align work with business priorities and ensure clear accountability, the CIDO Program Manager (PM) function is organized by divisional business unit and solution, enabling teams to focus on the specific needs of each business area while driving consistent, scalable delivery of IT capabilities.

  

The CIDO PM will report to the Missile Defense Integration (MDI) Business Unit CIDO PM and will serve as the primary liaison representing the Space Sector PMO, supporting multiple sites and programs across the Colorado Front Range region aligned to the business. This role provides CIDO leadership to technical teams delivering innovative information technology and security solutions in satisfaction of program requirements.

  

The CIDO PM works closely with other Functions and Shared Services teams, including Classified Solutions, Facilities, Physical Security, InfoSec/Cyber Security, Infrastructure Services, IT Operations, and Application Services, to securely deploy, maintain, and optimize IT services that enable enterprise classified and unclassified operations. jobs.description:
KPMG Advisory practice is currently our fastest growing practice. We are seeing tremendous client demand, and looking forward we do not anticipate that slowing down. In this ever-changing market environment, our professionals must be adaptable and thrive in a collaborative, team-driven culture. At KPMG, our people are our number one priority. With a wealth of learning and career development opportunities, a world-class training facility and leading market tools, we make sure our people continue to grow both professionally and personally. If you're looking for a firm with a strong team connection where you can be your whole self, have an impact, advance your skills, deepen your experiences, and have the flexibility and access to constantly find new areas of inspiration and expand your capabilities, then consider a career in Advisory.

KPMG is currently seeking a Director, IT TMT M&A - Due Diligence, Integration and Separation – Strategy to join our KPMG Strategy practice.

Responsibilities:

Manage and oversee comprehensive Buy-Side and Sell-Side assessments across critical IT domains for potential client acquisitions, with a focus on technology platforms, media content delivery networks, and telecommunications infrastructure; identify key IT risks, opportunities, and investments needed, and deliver executive-level due diligence reports with strategic recommendations
Direct IT integration and separation initiatives from planning through execution for TMT-related transactions, including software/SaaS, digital media, and telecom services; oversee development of IT current state assessments, entanglement identification, operating model definitions, synergies, and Day 1 and post-close plans and lead execution engagements including the implementation of ERP, HRIS, CRM, Microsoft 365 and other business applications platforms
Develop and execute go-to-market strategies for Technology M&A offerings focused on software, digital media, telecom, platform modernization, and ecosystem integration; provide thought leadership on TMT architectures, including cloud-native platforms, SaaS, content delivery networks (CDNs), and 5G/telecom infrastructure
Establish and manage program governance frameworks, ensuring rigorous oversight of execution across complex, multi-vendor TMT environments; lead development of governance work products including status reporting, risk management, and issue tracking; implement AI-powered tools for predictive analytics on project timelines and risks and collaborate with senior cross-functional teams to identify technology dependencies, risks, and opportunities across technology operations, product, engineering, and content/broadcast operations
Lead strategic discussions and presentations with executive IT and business stakeholders, including CIOs, CTOs, Chief Product Officers, and leaders in engineering and content
Lead efforts to mentor and develop junior staff, fostering deep TMT expertise and delivery excellence across the team

Qualifications:

Minimum eight years of recent experience in technology/business consulting and/or technology leadership, with a proven track record of leading IT transformations and advising on complex M&A transactions
Bachelor's degree in information systems, computer science, finance, or a related field from an accredited college/university required; advanced degree (MBA or equivalent) is preferred
Demonstrated success in leading high-impact IT-focused M&A projects with expertise in at least three of the following: system integration/separation, cloud platform migration, digital media workflow optimization, telecom network integration, or IT architecture modernization; advanced program management skills, with the capacity to oversee large, complex projects and deliver strategic insights to executive audiences; familiarity with leveraging AI-powered platforms for due diligence, synergy analysis, and integration planning is a significant plus
Proven track record leading complex technology M&A engagements (pre- and post-deal) within the Technology, Media, and Telecom (TMT) industry; in-depth knowledge of the technology and regulatory landscape specific to TMT, including experience with SaaS platforms, content delivery networks (CDNs), ad-tech, broadcast systems, or telecommunications infrastructure (e.g., 5G, fiber) and the IT implications of regulatory requirements from bodies like the FCC and data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA)
Comprehensive understanding of IT best practices and enterprise IT ecosystems, including major ERP, CRM, HRIS, and other business application platforms, IT solutions, systems, infrastructure, and cybersecurity; experience in the selection and implementation of Tier 1 or 2 service-centric ERP systems with broad knowledge across core finance modules supporting Order to Cash required; knowledge of supply chain and product-centric functionality helpful but not required
Strong strategic thinking and leadership abilities with experience developing and executing IT strategies that align with business objectives; experience developing and executing go-to-market strategies and driving business growth in the M&A space, including client relationship management and engagement in business development activities; proven ability to lead and mentor cross-functional teams
Willingness and ability to travel as needed to serve client needs
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. KPMG LLP will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa)

Technology Strategy Principal Director -- Insurance Industry

We Are:

Technology Strategy and Advisory and we design and execute industry-relevant reinventions that allow organizations to realize exceptional business value from technology. Our vision is to become the world’s leading advisors
in harnessing technology and innovation as a force to reinvent and improve every business. Our mission is to architect and realize exceptional value
from technology for our clients.

Technology Strategy leverages deep technology expertise, empowering clients to be more competitive by leading initiatives that develop pioneering, technology-enabled strategies that unlock value and drive growth. To stay agile in a world dominated by change, the C-suite must build new business architectures that break away from old ways of doing things, giving them the agility to compete and grow in the new. Accenture Technology Strategy enables leaders to act quickly and confidently as they pivot to the future. Known for our ability to execute at speed, we develop new capabilities in areas including Applied Intelligence, data and analytics, blockchain, robotics, Internet of Things and cyber

You Are:

A Technology Strategy Thought Leader & Expert with tons of top-flight leadership experience in technology and management skills, with embedded relationships and experience in the Financial Services Banking sector. You have deep, differentiated skills and expertise that are in high demand and relevant in the market. You have energy and drive in abundance, along with personal resilience, a passion for serving clients, and a love of continual learning. As a senior leader, you’re a natural at appreciating diverse perspectives and bringing out the best in teams, while also establishing credibility & confidence with C-Suite client leaders. As a Principal Director, you demonstrate “the four Cs” to the fullest:

Credentials – you have a proven track record of consistently delivering high value work.

Capability – you can show meaningful contribution to assets and practice areas.

Connections – you have evidence of C-Suite relevance and demonstrated ability to build senior client relationships.

Content – you have demonstrated ability to contribute, build, and lead thought capital.

The Work:

Lead complex projects to make sure clients are positioned for long-term success with practical road maps for carrying out Digital, IT or Cloud strategy, managing change, monitoring and gauging processes, and taking remedial steps.

Earn the trust of senior leaders at client organizations and partner with them to create strategic solutions at the intersection of business, technology, and operations.

Build relationships with clients to raise Accenture’s profile as a long-term trusted advisor and partner

Strengthen Accenture’s Technology Strategy practice and role as a thought leader by creating content and taking part in professional forums, both internal and external.

Drive and lead projects that deliver world-class business technology strategy solutions.

Mentor junior members of the Strategy team and prepare them for more responsibility. economic, technology, and social trends.

Travel as needed.

Here is what you need:

Minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in Technology Strategy, including at least 8 years in a management or leadership role driving technology-led business transformation within the Financial Services/Banking Industry.

Minimum of 8 years of experience in management or strategy consulting, with a proven track record of shaping and delivering complex technology strategy engagements for C-suite clients Including deep expertise in at least two of the following Technology Strategy domains:

Operating Model Design & Technology Architecture Strategy

Technology M&A / Post-Merger Integration Strategy

Technology Value Realization and Cost Take-Out

Cloud, Data, or AI-Enabled Transformation Strategy

Technology-Driven Revenue Growth or Platform Modernization

Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.

Bonus Points If:

You have a proven ability to lead high-performing teams, structure complex problem-solving efforts, and translate business strategy into actionable technology initiatives.

Demonstrated experience developing and presenting business cases (both quantitative and qualitative) to support major strategic initiatives or technology investments.

Recognized as a Thought Leader or Subject Matter Expert in Technology Strategy for Financial Services — evidenced by one or more of the following:

Publishing thought leadership or research papers

jobs.description:
We Are:

Accenture is a global professional services company with leading capabilities in digital, cloud and security. Combining unmatched experience and specialized skills across more than 40 industries, we offer Strategy and Consulting, Interactive, Technology and Operations services - all powered by the world's largest network of Advanced Technology and Intelligent Operations centers. Over 500,000 people deliver on the promise of technology and human ingenuity every day, serving clients in more than 120 countries. We embrace the power of change to create value and shared success for our clients, people, shareholders, partners and communities. Visit us at www.accenture.com.

You Ar
e:

A tolling technology leader with deep expertise in electronic toll collection, back-office and roadside systems, multi-lane free-flow (MLFF) technology, interoperability frameworks, and large-scale tolling modernization. You understand how to help agencies and infrastructure operators deploy, integrate, and evolve complex tolling technology platforms while balancing operational performance, financial objectives, customer expectations, regulatory requirements, and cybersecurity considerations. You have led significant technology portfolios, built executive relationships with agencies and vendors, developed market growth strategies, and created high-performing delivery organizations. You are a trusted advisor who can shape complex technology opportunities, mobilize multidisciplinary engineering and consulting teams, and translate tolling industry challenges into practical, scalable solutions. You combine deep technical credibility, commercial acumen, and delivery discipline with a passion for advancing safer, more efficient, and revenue-optimized tolling operations.

The Wor
k:

Lead the growth and expansion of Accenture's Smart Mobility Hub tolling technology portfolio across North America, with a focus on back-office modernization, roadside systems, and interoperability platforms.

Develop and maintain executive relationships with tolling agencies, transportation authorities, state departments of transportation, concessionaires, and infrastructure operators.

Originate, qualify, shape, and support closure of strategic tolling technology opportunities, including back-office platform replacements, MLFF deployments, interoperability integrations, and end-to-end system modernizations.

Serve as an executive sponsor and delivery advisor for complex modernization programs, providing oversight of outcomes, governance, financial performance, risk, and client satisfaction.

Lead and grow Accenture’s customer service operations technology practice within the tolling portfolio, encompassing contact center platforms, CRM systems, self-service digital channels, workforce management tools, omnichannel customer engagement, and AI-powered service automation for tolling agencies and operators.

Shape technology offerings across tolling back-office modernization (CSC, violations, collections), roadside and MLFF systems, electronic payment and account management platforms, customer service operations technology, interoperability hubs, revenue assurance, cybersecurity, data analytics, and AI/ML enablement for tolling operations.

Build reusable Smart Mobility Hub technology assets, reference architectures, delivery methods, accelerators, tolling platform solution narratives, and industry credentials to accelerate client pursuits.

Collaborate across Strategy & Consulting, Technology, Operations, Industry X, Song, and ecosystem partners to create integrated client solutions.

Lead industry thought leadership through client forums, conferences, associations, publications, and executive roundtables.

Recruit, mentor, and develop tolling technology practitioners — including systems architects, integration engineers, and platform specialists — while strengthening succession planning and technical industry capability.

Bring disciplined portfolio management, forecasting, and operational governance to pursuits and delivery programs.

A minimum of 12 years of experience in tolling technology, electronic toll collection, transportation systems integration, back-office platforms, roadside technology, or a closely related infrastructure technology field.

A minimum of 8 years of experience leading large-scale tolling technology modernization programs, systems integration delivery organizations, technology consulting engagements, or complex multi-vendor implementation programs.

Demonstrated experience managing executive client relationships and engaging with C-suite, agency, authority, or senior public-sector leaders.

Demonstrated experience shaping business opportunities, strategic pursuits, proposals, or market growth initiatives.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years' work experience). If Associate’s Degree, must have equivalent minimum 6-year work experience

Bonus Points If:

You have leadership of major transportation technology portfolios or multi-program delivery organizations with P&L, forecasting, margin, or cash-flow accountability.

You have hands-on experience with electronic toll collection technology, commercial or operational back-office systems, MLFF/AET roadside deployments, transponder and license plate recognition systems, interoperability protocols (e.g., E-ZPass, ETAN), violations processing, collections workflow, or revenue assurance platforms.

You have experience with public-private partnerships, concessions, design-build, or multidisciplinary system integration programs.

You have experience applying AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, computer vision, cloud-native architectures, or enterprise platforms to improve tolling technology delivery, revenue optimization, or operational performance.

You have experience leading PMO transformation, ERP adoption, enterprise governance, organizational change, or workforce development.

You have active participation or leadership in IBTTA, ITS America, AASHTO, or related transportation industry organizations.

You have advanced degree or relevant certifications such as PMP, PgMP, SAFe, or equivalent.

Posted Date 9/29/2026
Description Director, Technical Program Manager \- Card Tech
Do you love driving complex technical initiatives and pioneering in the technology space? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast\-paced, collaborative, inclusive, and iterative delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors, who love to solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Technical Program Managers who are passionate about marrying technology with business strategy to join our team. As a Technical Program Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to be on the forefront of driving major technical transformations and scaling platform capabilities across Capital One.

  

  

**About the Team:**


Digital Commerce \& Innovation (DCI) is a portfolio of technology platforms and solutions which support both enterprise and premium LOBs and delights our customers while revolutionizing the way our customers use and love our products and the industry at the same time. We will find synergies and efficiencies across the portfolio while driving autonomy, velocity, and agility as first principles. DCI domains include:


* **Spend Innovation** \- Our team operates at the entry point for customer experience by delivering seamless spending technology. From onboarding users and digital payments to spend management and external integrations, we power high\-trust transactions and actionable insights that drive real value for our customers.
* **Loyalty** \- We power personalized and interconnected rewards and benefits for all Capital One customers. We incentivize and reward customers for their use of Capital One credit cards and products, aiming to attract customers, increase usage, and enhance retention by fostering active engagement with rewards and benefits.
* **Travel Tech** \- We deliver and scale brand\-defining experiences across Travel. We provide travel booking services, rewards, and benefits to Capital One customers. By supporting our strategic business goal to win at the top of the market we’re enabling next\-level growth for Capital One.
* **Card Premium Experiences** \- We create world\-class experiences for our premium customers, including: AI, Concierge, dining, entertainment, lounges, and multi\-user features. Together we create unmatched value in Capital One’s premium offerings.

In addition to leading a top priority technical program for DCI, you will also work to pave the way for an expanding TPM discipline within the team, by leveraging your industry knowledge and experience to teach the organization what a great TPM can achieve.

  

  

**What You’ll Do:**


As a Director of Technical Program Management (TPM), we’re looking for someone that can help us lead programs that deliver on critical business goals and build large scale products \& platforms that will help Capital One customers have incredible experiences.

  

  

In addition to the technical program, you will also work to pave the way for an expanding TPM discipline within the team, by leveraging your industry knowledge and experience to teach the organization what a great TPM can achieve.

  

  

* Contribute to the organization’s TPM / Delivery strategy: establish operating mechanisms, maturity models, and tooling that scale across portfolios
* Drive development of and alignment on program roadmap anchored in business objectives, definition of done, technical solutions, and sequencing of dependencies
* Lead cross\-platform technical investment planning and ensure architectural alignment toward long\-term platform convergence and reuse
* Serve as an executive\-level escalation point for program risks, influencing technology leaders to make data\-driven tradeoffs between speed, cost and resiliency
* Ensure definition of measurable outcomes of platform success (availability, scalability, cost efficiency, developer velocity) and ensure delivery accountability across multiple engineering teams
  

  

**Basic Qualifications:**


* Bachelor's degree in a technical field
* At least 7 years of experience managing technical programs
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**


* 7\+ years of experience designing and building solutions using distributed computing or service oriented architecture (SOA)
* 3\+ years of experience in building distributed systems \& highly available services using cloud computing services / architecture \- preferably using AWS
* 3\+ years experience building highly scalable products \& platforms
* 3\+ years of experience with Agile delivery
* 3\+ years years experience delivering large and complex programs \- where you contribute to the business or technical vision, collaborate with large cross\-functional teams, secure commitments on deliverables and unblock teams to land business impact
* Experience in building systems \& solutions within a highly regulated environment
* MBA or Master’s Degree in a related technical field (Computer Science, Software Engineering)
* PMP, Lean, Agile, or Six Sigma certification
* 3\+ years of people management experience or influencing organization as an IC
* Experience driving platform standardization across multiple product portfolios or lines of business
* Track record of building TPM maturity (operating models, career frameworks, metrics) at scale within engineering organizations
* Exceptional communication and influence skills, capable of engaging deeply with technical teams while translating implications into compelling business narratives that persuade senior leadership
  

  

***At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization, or offer any immigration related support for this position (e.g. H1B, F\-1 OPT, F\-1 STEM OPT, F\-1 CPT, J\-1, TN, E\-3, and O\-1, or any other forms of work authorization that require immigration support from an employer).***

Posting Description:

Are you a Program Manager (non\-technical) ready for a change in your career? This could be a phenomenal opportunity to explore!  

We are seeking talent to support Aon Business Services (ABS) in a multi‑year strategic Operating Model Transformation. Reporting to the Director of Program Management for partnering closely with an Internal Consulting team and collaborators across the enterprise, this role is responsible for running the governance, planning and performance management framework that enables successful delivery of the transformation across solution lines, regions, and functions.  

This is a **hybrid role** with the flexibility to work both virtually and from one of our US offices.**Aon is in the business of better decisions**
----------------------------------------------


At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed!**What the day will look like**
-------------------------------

**Key Responsibilities**
Program Planning \& Delivery Management
* Build and maintain the collaborative transformation roadmap, including scope, achievements, critical path, and interdependencies across workstreams
* Facilitate identification, assessment, prioritization, and mitigation of program risks and dependencies, ensuring regulatory, compliance and operational risks are considered in all program activities
* Raise critical risks and recommended solutions to senior collaborators, and partner with workstream leads to baseline plans, monitor progress, and implement corrective actions where delivery risks emerge
* Drive planning, measurement and tracking of progress and benefits realization, ensuring alignment to the defined argument and strategic outcomes
* Support resource planning and allocation within assigned projects, including tracking team capacity and flagging resource constraints

**Program Governance \& Control**
---------------------------------

* Enable and maintain the governance framework for the operating model transformation, including steering committees, program approvals, and design workshops
* Define and administer standards, templates, and processes for program planning, status reporting, risk/issue management, and change control
* Ensure decisions, actions, and dependencies are documented, tracked, and resolved in a timely manner
* Manage the program calendar, including steering meetings, forums, and key decision achievements

**Collaborator Management \& Communication**
--------------------------------------------

* Cultivate positive relationships with business leaders, key collaborators, and cross\-functional partners to ensure agreement and engagement in transformation roadmap
* Develop and implement a clear communication and reporting strategy tailored to executive sponsors, business leaders, and delivery teams
* Produce high\-quality program reporting (e.g., dashboards, status reports, executive packs) that provide clear insight into progress, risks, and decisions needed
* Support change management activities in partnership with Change/HR/Communications teams, including impact assessments and engagement plans

**Change Enablement \& Continuous Improvement**
-----------------------------------------------

* Support changes and redesigns to the target operating model, including processes, organization, governance, and technology impacts, when challenges arise
* Ensure that design decisions are traceable to strategic objectives and translated into clear implementation plans
* Help define and monitor adoption and readiness metrics (e.g., training completion, process adherence, stabilization key performance indicators)
* Coordinate pilots, phased rollouts, and post‑implementation reviews, incorporating lessons learned into future releases
* Continuously refine PMO processes based on feedback, metrics, and lessons learned

**Skills and experience that will lead to success**
---------------------------------------------------

* 5\+ years of proven experience in project/program management, preferably with a consulting firm
* Hands‑on experience establishing Global Capability Centers (GCCs) or Centers of Excellence (COEs), including operating model design, process transition, and governance framework setup
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, multi‑workstream transformation programs (e.g., operating model redesign, shared services, process re‑engineering, or large‑scale systems implementation)
* Experience supervising or managing people.
* Experience working in a matrixed, global organization with senior executive collaborators

Additional Skills and Competencies:
Discretion and Impact, Complexity and Problem Solving, Collaboration and Interaction, Organization Skills, Communication  

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. **Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.**  

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.**Pay Transparency Laws:**

====================

  

PACS Group, Inc. is a holding company investing in post\-acute healthcare facilities, professionals, and ancillary services. Founded in 2013, PACS Group is one of the largest post\-acute platforms in the United States. PACS business support division, PACS Services, provides technology and administrative support services — accounting, finance, human resources, compliance, payroll, AR/AP, legal, risk management, information technology, corporate communication, and other business advice and support — to their healthcare facilities, reducing administrative burdens so their leadership and care teams can focus on the care, well\-being, and quality of life of their patients and residents. Building a world where LGBT people thrive as healthy, equal, and complete members of society.

**DEPARTMENT SUMMARY**


The IT department supports the organization's technology infrastructure and systems, focusing on delivering reliable, secure, and scalable technology solutions. It drives enterprise\-wide technology modernization and supports operational efficiency through strategic technology management and innovation.

**JOB SUMMARY**


The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) leads enterprise\-wide technology modernization efforts within the IT department, focusing on stabilizing and optimizing the OCHIN Epic system to ensure effective delivery on technology investments. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, the CTO directs technology strategy, resource management, and innovation initiatives to enhance the end\-user experience and operational efficiency across the organization. This role provides leadership to the Head of Technology and ITS/HIS teams and manages technology budgets and purchasing decisions.

 **ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**


Technology Strategy and Leadership  

* Develop and execute the organization's technology strategy aligned with operational and infrastructure objectives, emphasizing enterprise\-wide modernization and OCHIN Epic system optimization.
* Lead technology change management initiatives to improve organizational effectiveness and service delivery, with a focus on healthcare technology expertise.
* Collaborate with executive leadership and cross\-functional teams to integrate technology solutions that support organizational goals and impact multiple functions.


  

 IT Systems and Infrastructure Management  

* Oversee the design, implementation, and maintenance of IT systems and infrastructure to ensure reliability, security, scalability, and compliance with relevant standards and regulations.
* Manage technology budgets, purchasing, resources, and vendor relationships to optimize investments and performance.


  

 Team Leadership and Development  

* Provide leadership, guidance, and professional development opportunities to IT teams, including the Head of Technology and ITS/HIS teams, fostering high performance and innovation.


  

 Operational Decision\-Making and Support  

* Make independent decisions regarding financial investments in technology solutions, team and department restructures, and implementation of new systems affecting the entire organization.
* Maintain availability for technology emergencies to ensure continuous operational support.


  

 Supervisory Responsibilities  

* Directly supervises the Head of Technology and ITS/HIS teams.
* Responsible for decisions involving team and department restructuring.
* Oversees staff development, performance management, and recruitment within supervised teams.
 **NON\-ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

* Perform other duties as assigned.

 **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
* Significant experience in technology leadership roles within complex organizations, including strategic planning, IT management, and technology implementation.
* Demonstrated expertise in OCHIN Epic/Epic system implementation and healthcare technology.
* Proven track record of managing enterprise\-wide technology modernization and change management initiatives.
* No license or certification is required.
* Proficiency in IT systems architecture, infrastructure management, cybersecurity principles, and technology project management.
* Experience with technology budgeting, purchasing, and vendor management.

jobs.title: CISO Support SME
jobs.description:
Since 1958, DARPA has made pivotal investments in breakthrough technologies for national security. As the world changes dramatically – and even the pace of change itself increases – the agency seeks to engage the best minds and best ideas across specialties, communities, and disciplines to solve the greatest national security challenges on the horizon. DARPA brings together scientists, engineers, and tinkerers across the innovation ecosystem to push the bounds of technological possibility. The work we do is challenging by nature, but working with DARPA doesn’t have to be.
To make it happen, DARPA's program managers need highly skilled support contractors, broadly referred to as SETAs (Scientific Engineering and Technical Assistance) within DARPA. Often spanning programs, portfolios, and even offices in their impact, the SETAs help program managers chart and navigate the path toward groundbreaking discoveries. For the fortunate few who become part of the DARPA legacy, a time bound journey with the organization represents a unique and singular opportunity to alter the future. At DARPA, every day is a chance to make history. A chance to explore, discover, and invent. A chance to collaborate with pioneers in science and engineering contributing to an enduring mission.
The CISO SME provides principal\-level advisory and thought leadership to senior DARPA executives, including the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and senior ITD Staff. As a Senior Senior Scientific, Engineering, and Technical Assistance (SETA), this position is a key strategic resource that helps shape the agency's approach to cybersecurity across its most advanced and sensitive technology portfolios.Requires a distinguished expert with extensive, deep experience in secure multi\-level cloud architectures, Cross Domain Solutions (CDS), and the complex security landscape of paradigm\-shifting technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI). Will operate with a high degree of autonomy to provide strategic foresight, critical technical analysis, and authoritative guidance, ensuring that security is an enabler of innovation for DARPA's high\-risk, high\-reward programs. The primary function is to serve as a top\-tier advisor, influencing the strategic direction of cybersecurity for the nation's next generation of breakthrough technologies.


Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

* Strategic Advisory \& Leadership: Provide principal\-level cybersecurity expertise and strategic counsel to DARPA senior leadership. Lead critical assessments and shape the agency's long\-term security roadmap for cloud and emerging technologies.
* Cloud \& CDS Architecture Authority: Serve as a leading authority on the evaluation of secure cloud architectures and Cross Domain Solutions. Provide definitive recommendations on designs for multi\-level, hybrid cloud, and highly sensitive environments, ensuring they are resilient, compliant, and mission capable.
* Emerging Technology Threat \& Opportunity Analysis: Drive analysis of the strategic security implications of nascent and future technologies. Develop and champion novel security frameworks and threat models for AI, quantum computing, and other areas of strategic interest to DARPA.
* Portfolio\-Level Cybersecurity Strategy: Guide Program Managers in the development of robust, portfolio\-wide cybersecurity strategies. Mentor performers and government staff on the integration of advanced security principles from program inception through technology transition.
* Independent Technical Validation: Lead independent technical assessments and validations of performer\-developed technologies. Provide clear, unbiased, and impactful recommendations to senior government leaders on the viability, security, and risk posture of proposed solutions.
* Senior\-Level Liaison and Influence: Act as a key liaison between the CISO’s office, program offices, and the broader national security R\&D community. Leverage deep professional relationships to foster collaboration and influence cybersecurity best practices.

**Mandatory Qualifications**

* Security Clearance: Must possess an active Top Secret (TS) security clearance with eligibility for Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI). Eligibility for SAP access and a counterintelligence scope polygraph may be required.
* Education: Master’s degree or Ph.D. in a relevant technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related discipline).
* Senior SETA Experience: A minimum of 15 years of progressive experience, with at least 6 years operating in a senior SETA, principal advisor, or chief architect capacity supporting DoD or Intelligence Community agencies.
* Technical Expertise:
* Authoritative expertise in architecting, securing, and assessing complex hybrid cloud and/or multi\-cloud environments (AWS, Azure) within secure government contexts.
* At least 5 years of technical experience in a Major Acquisition Program Office in the DoW.
* Extensive and deep practical experience with the architecture, approval process (e.g., UCDSMO), and operational management of Cross Domain Solutions (CDS).
* Profound understanding of the security challenges and opportunities presented by emerging technologies, particularly AI/ML.
* Mastery of DoD cybersecurity policies, the Risk Management Framework (RMF), and NIST security standards.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience: Extensive experience providing direct SETA support to DARPA or a similar high\-paced R\&D organization, Recognized as a subject matter expert in cloud security, CDS, or AI security within the DoD or Intelligence Community, and Extensive experience briefing and advising Flag Officers, Senior Executive Service (SES) members, and other senior government leaders.
* Strategic Vision: Demonstrated ability to anticipate future technology and threat trends and develop long\-range strategic plans to address them.

This position carries a strong level of responsibility and requires the ability to manage day\-to\-day execution while escalating risks, blockers, and process gaps where needed. * **Build Support:** Partner with construction, engineering, logistics, operations, and regional inventory teams to align material flow and inventory readiness with local build schedules.
* **System Accuracy \& Compliance:** Ensure inventory transactions, movements, reconciliations, and deployments are captured accurately within Oracle systems; maintain records to support audit and compliance requirements.

* **Governance Support:** Apply global inventory policies and regional operating procedures while ensuring compliance with security, safety, audit, and operational standards.

**Required Skills \& Experience**

* **Program / Project Coordination:** Experience supporting cross\-functional projects or programs with measurable outcomes in a fast\-paced operational environment.
* **Inventory Management Knowledge:** Good understanding of material flow, inventory accuracy, reconciliation, stock control, and audit requirements.
* **3PL / Vendor Support:** Experience working with logistics providers, warehouse teams, or vendors to support SLA adherence, inventory movement, and operational execution.
* **Analytical Skills:** Ability to review inventory data, identify discrepancies or trends, and support corrective actions.
* **Risk \& Issue Awareness:** Able to identify risks early, communicate blockers clearly, and support mitigation activities to maintain project alignment.
* **Communication \& Collaboration:** Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with regional peers, site teams, vendors, and cross\-functional partners.

jobs.title: Program Manager V
jobs.description:
The purpose of this position is to be a Senior Advisor to the Division Manager of the Homeland Security Division which is a unit of up to 10 full time employees, within the Office of Grants and Research (OGR), that is primarily responsible for managing and administering federal funds received from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), such as the Homeland Security Grant Program, comprised of the State Homeland Security Program and Urban Areas Security Initiative (UASI), Nonprofit Security Grant, State and Local Cyber Security Investment Program, as well as other state and federal grant programs as assigned by the Executive Director. The Division is also responsible for coordinating and completing the Threat and Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (THIRA) as well as the Stakeholder Preparedness Review (SPR), as required by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The Senior Advisor assists the Division Manager and works with the Special Projects Manager by attending critical meetings upon request as it relates to this funding portfolio, which may include but not limited to the UASI Working Group, State Interoperability Executive Committee, Boston Area Maritime Security Council, and other homeland security related forums.


It is the responsibility of the Senior Advisor to assist the Division Manager with ensuring that homeland security activities are 1\) coordinated among internal and external entities, including state agencies, local government entities, and the homeland security planning regions and 2\) consistent with the goals and objectives of the Commonwealth's State Homeland Security Strategy, and 3\) support closing capability gaps or sustaining capabilities, as identified in the THIRA/SPR. This position is critical to the implementation of the Commonwealth's strategy toward enhancing interactions with the federal, regional and local partners to protect the people who live in, work in and visit the Commonwealth from future acts of terrorism or other catastrophic events. The Senior Advisor will ensure that funded homeland security efforts statewide will proceed in a coordinated, consistent manner, adhering to the central homeland security strategy. The primary purpose of this role is to assist the Division Manager and division staff by ensuring that all federal and state grant administration rules and regulations are being met; identify and recommend improvements to OGR's grants management processes; ensure all federal reporting requirements are being met, provide guidance and support to staff managing subrecipients, and find, apply for and secure new competitive homeland security related grant opportunities on behalf of the Commonwealth.

* Supervise staff assigned and assist with the administration of DHS and other related federal and state grant programs and ensure internal and external compliance with rules and regulations. This is accomplished by working with the team on developing spending and programmatic guidelines for OGR sub\-recipients and reinforcing state appropriation language; developing and implementing policies regarding proper procurement, reimbursement, and reporting; and reviewing grant applications and delivering funding recommendations to the Executive Director of OGR
* Upon request of the Division Manager, coordinate state homeland security related activities with other local, regional, state, and federal entities. This is accomplished by working with the staff to assist locals and regions with the development and implementation of mutual aid agreements, training and exercise programs, emergency operation plans, response and recovery plans, emergency communications plans, and continuity of operations plans via funding and technical assistance; conducting bi\-weekly conference calls and meeting at least quarterly with homeland security regions to reinforce the state and national homeland security priorities and share relevant information/resources; developing goals and funding guidelines for state agencies and authorities to implement statewide homeland security efforts such as information sharing, resource database development, chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosive detection, mitigation and response; coordinating the evaluation and implementation of upgrades, as necessary, to information communications and other technology capabilities; conduct coordinated stakeholder engagement and data collection among multiple stakeholders to update the THIRA/SPR, as required

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a hands-on, multi-disciplinary Chief Technology Officer to lead its end-to-end technology organization, spanning product engineering, IT infrastructure, and corporate and platform cybersecurity.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and partnering with executive leadership, this executive provides comprehensive oversight across technology, enterprise systems, and risk management. The Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer reports directly to this role.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Drive overall technology strategy, cloud infrastructure, and technical execution for the organization's core SaaS platform.
Manage the enterprise technology budget and drive cost optimization across software licensing, infrastructure procurement, hardware lifecycles, and vendor contracts.
Partner with executive leadership to transition new products from beta to market launch while actively managing technical debt.
Advise the CEO and Board of Directors on enterprise technical risk, disaster recovery, business continuity planning, and corporate cyber resilience.
Oversee day-to-day corporate IT operations, including endpoint management, automated provisioning and deprovisioning, and multi-tier helpdesk support.
Administer enterprise productivity suites and communication architectures while enforcing zero-trust access controls, single sign-on (SSO), and document retention policies.
Oversee business system infrastructure in close alignment with organizational leadership to ensure high uptime and integration security.
Direct organization-wide information security initiatives across corporate endpoints, networks, and SaaS tools.
Establish and audit enterprise IT policies, including acceptable use, zero-trust identity and access management (IAM), data loss prevention (DLP), and offboarding protocols.
Enforce compliance and audit readiness—including SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, ISO 27001, and c3/c4 non-profit legal boundaries—in collaboration with Legal, HR, and Finance.
Evaluate alpha projects and proofs of concept across departments, guiding execution to integrate them into the core SaaS platform or architect them as standalone, scalable services.
Mitigate vendor lock-in risk by establishing standardized data portability and integration frameworks across corporate SaaS applications.
Serve as direct manager to the Chief Product, Engineering, and Data Officer (CPEDO), establishing shared goals and aligning product, engineering, and data strategies with enterprise infrastructure and security standards.
Partner with the CPEDO on budget, resourcing, and prioritization trade-offs across product, engineering, and data initiatives.
Build, mentor, and scale a service-oriented IT and security team aligned with organizational growth objectives.
Establish pragmatic automated internal processes that maintain rigorous security standards without introducing operational friction for staff.

Qualifications

12+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, including roles such as Director of IT, Head of IT/Operations Technology, VP of IT, or Chief Technology Officer.
Demonstrated experience managing enterprise IT and information security stacks, zero-trust architectures, IAM, and automated endpoint management.
Experience driving capital and operational expenditure (CapEx/OpEx) strategies for corporate IT, including SaaS license management, hardware procurement cycles, and third-party vendor governance.
Proven track record leading enterprise security operations and successfully navigating SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 audit cycles.
Expertise in architecting, securing, and administering enterprise collaboration platforms and workplace productivity suites.
Proven track record of building and leading technical teams across a broad range of expertise.
Experience building or scaling an internal IT function through periods of organizational growth.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical staff, executive leadership, and Board members.

Annual salary: $220,000 to $230,000,
commensurate with experience.
Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Healthcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) options.
403(b) retirement plan with an employer match.
Paid vacation, paid holidays, and paid sick leave.
Paid parental leave.
Professional development and education reimbursement assistance.
Monthly technology and wellness stipend.

Essential duties reflect the primary functions assigned to this role and may be adjusted or reassigned at any time.
Employees must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations will be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions, absent undue hardship.
The organization maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding abuse and inappropriate behavior.
